requirements: Proficiency in Java, C, Go, or Python and strict adherence to rules against using AI or external assistance.

title: Threws Odyssey 2026
description: THREWS ODYSSEY 2026 is an online research and innovation hackathon where participants build practical technology-based solutions for real-world problems. It features multiple tracks ranging from Artificial Intelligence to Web3 and Open Innovation.
eligibility: Open to college students, freshers, professionals, researchers, and independent developers, participating individually or in teams of up to two.
requirements: Submissions must include a project name, problem statement, solution description, tech stack, source code, and a working prototype or demonstration.
details_text: Overview THREWS ODYSSEY 2026 is an online research and innovation hackathon organised by Threws – The Research World. The hackathon brings together students, developers, researchers and technology enthusiasts to build practical solutions to real-world problems across multiple domains. Participants can choose a problem from one of the following tracks: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Medical & HealthTech Cybersecurity FinTech ClimateTech & Sustainability DeepTech & Scientific Computing Smart Cities & Social Impact Human-AI & Assistive Technology Web3, Privacy & Decentralised Systems Open Innovation What to Build Participants are expected to identify a meaningful problem and develop a working solution. Projects can be software products, AI/ML systems, research prototypes, cybersecurity solutions, data-driven applications or other technology-based solutions relevant to the selected track. Projects should demonstrate a clear problem statement, a well-defined approach and a functional prototype. Participants are encouraged to research existing solutions and explain how their approach improves upon or differs from them. Eligibility Open to college students, freshers, professionals, researchers and independent developers. Participants from any academic or technical background can apply. Participation is open to individuals as well as teams. Maximum team size: 2 members. Participants may choose any one of the available tracks. Hackathon Process Register for THREWS ODYSSEY 2026. Select a track and identify a problem. Develop the solution during the hackathon period. Test and refine the project. Submit the project before the submission deadline. Submissions will be reviewed by the judging panel. Shortlisted participants may be invited for a final demonstration or presentation. Winners will be announced after the final evaluation. Submission Requirements Each submission must include: Project name Problem statement Description of the proposed solution Key features Technology stack Source code / repository Working prototype or demonstration Brief explanation of the implementation Dataset and external resources used, where applicable Results or evaluation, where applicable A short demo video may also be requested for shortlisted projects. Judging Projects will be evaluated on: Innovation and originality Technical implementation Relevance and importance of the problem Quality of the solution Research, experimentation and use of data where applicable Potential impact and scalability Quality of the final demonstration Rules Submissions must be the original work of the participating individual or team. Pre-existing projects may be used as a starting point only if substantial new work is carried out during the hackathon and clearly disclosed. Participants may use open-source libraries, APIs, datasets and development tools, subject to their respective licences. Use of AI coding and research tools is permitted. Participants must understand the work submitted under their name and be able to explain it during evaluation. All third-party resources must be properly acknowledged. Plagiarism, copied submissions, fabricated results or misrepresentation of work may result in disqualification. Each participant may be part of only one team. Projects must comply with applicable laws, licences and ethical standards. The organisers reserve the right to reject submissions that do not meet the eligibility or submission requirements. The decision of the judging panel will be final. The objective of THREWS ODYSSEY is simple: find meaningful problems, explore better solutions and build something that can make a difference. Build something worth discovering. Prizes & Recognition Total Prize Pool: ₹1,50,000

title: Code Auction
organiser: Guru Tegh Bahadur 4th Centenary Engineering College, Delhi
description: Code Auction is a team-based competitive coding event that combines programming with strategic, auction-based decision-making. Teams bid virtual currency on problems and utilize Power Cards to maximize their final scores.
eligibility: Teams consisting of 2–4 members.
requirements: A team of 2–4 members and strategic management of allocated token currency.
details_text: Overview Code Auction is a team-based competitive coding event. It combines programming, strategy, and auction-based decision-making, where teams bid virtual currency on programming problems and strategically manage their resources to maximize their scores. Event Date: 22nd October 2026 Guidelines Each team must consist of 2–4 members . All team members can discuss and solve the purchased problems. Each team receives an equal amount of token currency. Teams must manage their currency strategically between programming problems and Power Cards. The event includes the following Power Cards: Extra Time: Provides additional time for an eligible problem. Hint: Provides a useful hint for an eligible problem. Double Points: Doubles the points earned from an eligible solved problem. Steal: Allows a team to claim an eligible advantage/problem under the event rules. Exact Power Card effects and usage conditions will be announced before the event. Correctly solved problems earn points, and problem difficulty may determine the points awarded. Power Cards may modify scores according to their stated effects. The guidelines do not specify whether inter-college or inter-specialization teams are allowed. The number of programming problems and the duration of individual rounds have not been specified. Rules Teams cannot bid more coins than their available balance. All bids must be placed within the announced bidding time. Power Cards can only be used according to their stated rules and usage conditions. Copying or using unauthorized assistance may lead to disqualification. The team with the highest final score will be declared the winner. The organizers' decision will be final and binding.

title: Keep Alive ’26
organiser: Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Nagpur
description: KEEP ALIVE '26 is a national incident response championship where DevOps students investigate microservices failures using an observability stack. Participants must identify root causes and propose fixes through a multi-stage competition.
eligibility: Teams of exactly three students from the same college (UG, PG, or diploma), including up to one recent graduate (2024–2026); PhD students are ineligible.
requirements: 6–12 months of DevOps experience (Linux, Docker, Kubernetes) and at least two laptops per team for the finale.
details_text: An alert just fired. Checkout is failing. Can your team find out why before the clock runs out? KEEP ALIVE '26 is a national incident response championship for students who have been learning DevOps. You've practised Linux, Docker and Kubernetes. Now test it on the field: read the alerts, dashboards, logs and traces of a live microservices system, find what broke and why, and explain how you would fix it. It runs on the same incident platform as Panic at the Pod, the live Kubernetes incident challenge by CNCG Noida , our Community Partner. KEEP ALIVE takes that format nationwide, built and scaled for students. It is hosted by GDG on Campus IIIT Nagpur at TantraFiesta 2026 , the national technical fest of IIIT Nagpur. Why take part ₹25,000 in cash prizes for the top three teams and the Sharpest RCA award Investigate real incidents on a real observability stack: Grafana dashboards, Prometheus metrics, logs and traces No production experience needed. A 30-minute hands-on session at the finale teaches every tool you will use After the finale, the platform team walks everyone through all 10 incidents and how they were solved Goodies and certificates for every finalist, and merit certificates for the winners Bring your senior: one recent graduate (2024 to 2026) of your college can join your team Round 1: The Night Shift (online, 11 to 18 October) One 30-minute assessment per team, taken once from the team leader's account Multiple-choice questions on DevOps and observability, one incident to investigate from screenshots of dashboards, logs and traces, and two short written answers Proctored and taken in full screen. No AI tools, no search and no second device The top 15 teams reach the finale. The next 10 teams form the waitlist Finale: KEEP ALIVE Live (on campus, 26 October, IIIT Nagpur) A hands-on session on the platform, Grafana and the report form, with one practice incident Phase 1, First Responder: 6 incidents in 90 minutes Phase 2, Deep Dive: 3 intermediate incidents and 1 critical, cascading incident in 90 minutes You never change the system. You read its signals and submit a short solution report for each incident: the root cause, the evidence and the fix Each team presents its findings to the judges in a 10-minute slot Who can join Teams of exactly 3, all from the same college UG, PG and diploma students from any branch or year Up to one alumnus per team, graduated in 2024, 2025 or 2026. Working alumni are welcome PhD students and research scholars are not eligible Made for students with atleast 6 to 12 months of DevOps learning: if you have used Linux and Docker, run kubectl and opened Grafana a few times, you are ready Important dates (IST) Registration closes: Sunday, 18 October, 11:29 PM Round 1 window: Sunday, 11 October, 9:00 AM to Sunday, 18 October, 11:59 PM Finalists and waitlist announced: Monday, 19 October, 6:00 AM Finalists confirm their seats: by Tuesday, 20 October, 11:59 PM Finale: Monday, 26 October, at IIIT Nagpur Prizes Winner: ₹12,000 1st runner-up: ₹7,000 2nd runner-up: ₹4,000 Sharpest RCA award: ₹2,000, for the most accurate root causes among teams outside the top 3 Good to know Travel and stay for the finale are arranged by each team. Every team brings at least 2 laptops AI tools, search and documentation are allowed in the finale, but every team must be able to explain what it submits

title: D3COY
organiser: Shri Vile Parle Kelavani Mandal's Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering (DJSCE), Mumbai
description: D3COY is a 24-hour national-level innovation hackathon focused on tackling real-world challenges in security, privacy, and digital trust. Participants will build resilient products and adapt to real-time constraints in a high-intensity adversarial environment.
eligibility: All undergraduate students from any branch or background; inter-college teams are permitted.
requirements: Teams of 2-4 members must pay a ₹200 registration fee and pass Round 0 by submitting a solution PPT and member resumes.
details_text: Welcome to D3COY: Outsmart the Obvious! D3COY is a 24-hour national-level innovation hackathon organized by the DJSISACA Student Chapter at DJSCE. This event brings together developers, designers, problem-solvers, and tech enthusiasts to tackle real-world challenges in security, privacy, and digital trust.The hackathon challenges participants to strip away the safety nets, think beyond conventional solutions, and develop resilient, technically sound products within a high-intensity 24-hour adversarial environment. You will not only build but also adapt in real-time to unscripted mid-event curveballs and live constraints.Participants will have the opportunity to showcase their technical skills, adaptability, creativity, and problem-solving abilities while competing with top teams from across partner colleges, all while being judged and mentored by industry professionals. Round 0 - PPT Screening (Selection Round) : The journey to D3COY begins with our online screening round. All teams will be provided with a single, common Problem Statement (PS) for Round 0. You will be evaluated based on your unique approach to solving this specific challenge. Selection will be based on: Quality and originality of the proposed solution (PPT submission based on the provided common Problem Statement). Technical understanding of the problem statement. Feasibility and potential impact of the proposed approach. Unique Selling Proposition (USP) and Future Scope, demonstrating what sets your idea apart and how it can be scaled or applied in the real world. Teams must submit their solution PPT and the resumes of all team members as part of the Round 0 submission. The top 36 shortlisted teams will earn the exclusive opportunity to advance to the on-site 24-hour hackathon at the DJSCE campus. Team Formation : Team Size: Minimum 2 and Maximum 4 members per team. Inter-College Teams: Allowed (Team members can be from different colleges). Each team must successfully complete the Round 0 registration and submission requirements. Registration Fee : Registration Fee: ₹200 per team. (Note: This entry fee applies only to the Round 0 selection phase. Teams that are shortlisted will not have to pay any additional fees for the main 24-hour offline hackathon). Accommodation, Meals & Perks (For Shortlisted Teams) : On-campus workspace and accommodation will be provided strictly for the 24-hour duration of the offline hackathon. Please note: No accommodation will be provided prior to the start of the event or after the event concludes. The 24-hour on-campus stay includes full meals, refreshments, and exclusive sponsor goodies/swag for all Who Can Participate  (For the Main 24-Hour Hackathon) D3COY is open to all undergraduate students from any branch or background. Whether you are a security enthusiast, an AI developer, or a general innovator, there is a track for you. For the final on-site hackathon, participants will build solutions in one of the following tracks: Network & Infrastructure Security: Build tools that defend shared,high-traffic systems from intrusion or abuse. AI/ML Security & Deception: Develop deepfake/spoof detection, adversarial-ML defense, and model integrity tooling. Data Privacy & Cryptography: Create secure storage, encryption tooling, and privacy-preserving data systems

Final Judging Criteria Technical implementation – 25% Functionality / working prototype – 20% Innovation – 15% Problem understanding – 10% Real-world impact – 10% Scalability – 5% UI/UX – 5% Presentation and communication – 5% GitHub development and code quality – 5% Total: 100% Rules and Regulations All teams must complete registration through Unstop. title: The Lost Pathways (A Micromouse Event)
organiser: Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Nagpur
description: Teams compete to engineer an autonomous MicroMouse robot that navigates a 16x16 maze to find the shortest path from a corner to the center. The goal is to complete the mission in the fastest time possible.
eligibility: Teams of 1–5 members.
requirements: An autonomous robot measuring no more than 16x16x10 cm, powered by onboard batteries (max 15V), without cameras or harmful mechanisms, and must pass technical inspection.
details_text: Introduction Teams must engineer an autonomous robot (MicroMouse) that can find the shortest path in a 16×16 maze from a specified start square to the destination square of the maze. Robots must map, learn, and optimize their path to the destination in the least time possible. Objective In this competition, the mission of the autonomous robot is to negotiate a maze from specified corner to its center in the shortest possible time. Technical Inspection and Registration The robot needs to pass technical inspection before the competition. The robot technical inspection is based on paragraphs “6.” and “9.”. During the inspection, it is checked whether the robot or the operator who is handling the robot meets the paragraphs requirements. Only one team member with a robot (the currently selected robot operator) can come to the technical inspection. The purpose of this is to guarantee a smooth course of the competition and technical inspection. Contest Eligibility Team size: 1–5 members. One operator and up to four assistants may be registered for each robot (maximum of five team members in total). The team may change the designated operator in accordance with the competition rules. Rules for the Robot The robot must be autonomous (no remote controls allowed). The robot must not leave any part of its body behind whilst solving the maze. The robot is not allowed to jump over, fly over, climb, scratch, cut, burn, mark, damage, or destroy the walls of the maze. The Robot must not be larger, either in length or in width, than 16 centimeters. The dimensions of a robot that changes its parameters during a run cannot expand larger than 16 cm × 16 cm. The height of the robot should be under 10cm. Power: Onboard batteries only, not exceeding 15V. The use of cameras or any device to scan or memorize the maze is strictly prohibited. No harmful mechanisms, pneumatics, hydraulics. Any violation of these rules will constitute immediate disqualification. Rules for the Maze The maze is composed of 18 cm × 18 cm unit squares and comprises up to 16 × 16 squares. The walls of the maze are 7 cm high and 1.2 cm thick (assume 5 % tolerance). The distance from wall to wall within a square is 16.8 cm. The outside wall encloses the entire maze. The sides of the maze walls are white, the tops of the walls may be red, and the floor is black, finished with matt colour. The walls may not be uniformly white, the tops of the walls may not be uniformly red, and the floor may not be uniformly black. Fading can occur, and parts from different mazes may be used. Also, the floor may not provide a consistent level of friction. The start of the maze is located at one of the four corners. The start square is bordered with walls on three sides. The start line is located between the first and the second square. The goal is to reach the target square located in the centre of the maze, which consists of an area made up of four 18 cm × 18 cm squares. The finish line is at the entrance of the target square. There are multiple paths to the target square, and contestants are expected to use them. The target square has only one entrance and it will be positioned so that a wall-hugging robot will not be able to find it. Rules for the Competition Each contesting robot is allocated a total of 20 minutes of access to the final maze. Any time used to adjust a robot between runs is included in the 20 minutes. Each run (from the start cell to the centre zone) in which a robot successfully reaches the target square is given a run time. The minimum run time shall be the official result of the robot. First place goes to the robot with the shortest official time. Second place to the next shortest, and so on. Robots that do not finish the maze will be ranked by how close they got to the destination square. Each run shall be made from the starting square. The operator may abort a run at any time. If an operator touches the robot during a run, it is deemed aborted, and the robot must be removed

title: Line-O-Mania | A Line Follower Competition
organiser: Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Nagpur
description: Line-O-Mania is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build bots to navigate a complex black-and-white line track featuring various obstacles. The goal is to complete the course in the shortest time possible while managing unpredictable track elements.
eligibility: Open to all teams, including inter-college teams; however, a participant cannot be in more than one team.
requirements: Autonomous robots (no pre-made kits or RC), maximum 12V DC, a designated team leader, and adherence to strict navigation and safety rules.
details_text: Line-O-Mania is a robotics contest where teams build autonomous robot capable of following a pre-defined path on a contrast background. The track will be black and white and include challenges such as bends, loop, sharp turns, junctions, dotted lines, and dead-ends. The bots will require precise navigation to reach the end point in the shortest possible time. In addition, a special element will be introduced in the track, which will be disclosed only on the day of the event, adding an extra layer of challenge and unpredictibility. Team Formation Rules: One participant cannot be in more than one team. Each team must have a unique team name. No restriction on the number of teams from a college. Inter-college teams are allowed. Only one member selected by the team will be allowed to perform hand touch to the bot (if required) Each team must appoint a Team Leader (all communication via leader). Team Leader must be present during the run. Track Specifications: Track layout will be disclosed on the spot. Line: 3cm wide on black and white contrast track. Start and end points will be different. Track material: Flex sheets made of PVC Bot Specifications: Robots must be completely autonomous, no remote controlled bots allowed. Pre-run inspection will be conducted. No pneumatics, hydraulics, or harmful mechanisms allowed. No pre-made kits or Lego kits permitted. Maximum DC voltage ≤ 12V between any two circuit points. If the bot malfunctions, a short repair timeout of 30 secs can be opted for. Runtime will resume after 30 seconds or whenever the team is ready. Conduction Rules: Damaging the arena will lead to instant disqualification. If the bot leaves the track or requires intervention → restart from the previous checkpoint. Only Five (5) such penalties are allowed. After the 5th penalty the bot will get disqualified. 1 minute allowed for sensor calibration before run; timer starts regardless after this. Violation of rules may lead to disqualification. The judge's decision will be final and binding. Misbehaviour will lead to immediate disqualification. Judging & Scoring: Scoring System: (600 - Time taken in seconds) - (Penalties + Skips) Bonus points for completing the track. Skipped checkpoints = time penalty Maximum 2 figures/obstacles can be skipped; beyond that, all figures/obstacles have to be cleared or the team may choose to end their run. If the bot exits the arena, the team will have to restart from their last checkpoint with a penalty. Note: Rules may be subject to change according to the circumstances

title: Glitched
organiser: Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering (FRCRCE), Bandra
description: GLITCHED is a multi-round competitive debugging event organized by GDA CRCE designed to test diagnostic speed and systems thinking under time pressure. The competition progresses from pseudo-code debugging to game debugging and a complex final challenge.
eligibility: Only FR CRCE students; inter-college team members are not allowed.

details_text: GLITCHED is a focused, multi-round competitive debugging event designed to test diagnostic speed, systems thinking, and practical fixability under time pressure . Organized by the Game Developers Association (GDA) CRCE . Guidelines: Team Size: Exactly 3 members per team (the team members must be from same year, branch and division). Eligibility: ONLY FR CRCE STUDENTS ARE ALLOWED . Inter-college Team Members: NOT A llowed . Number of Rounds & Problem Statements: Round 1 (Qualification - Online Platform): Pseudo-code debugging involving multiple problem statements, game visuals, and pseudo-code . Round 2 (Game Debugging): Project/game files containing functional bugs to locate and fix . Final Round (Finals Challenge): A complex final project containing interconnected systems and cascading bugs . Duration & Structure: 2 Days of competitive debugging (Day 1: Qualification Rounds 1 & 2; Day 2: Finals) . Elimination Flow: All registered teams  Round 1 (50% qualify) to Round 2 (6–8 teams or 30% qualify) to Final Challenge (1 Winner & 1 Runner-up,1 FE Winner ) . Rules & Regulations: Fair Play: Teams must work exclusively on their assigned project/environment. Intentionally damaging, interfering with, or sabotaging another team's project or system will lead to immediate disqualification . Scope Control: Teams may modify only the specific files or components permitted by the organizers for each round . AI & Internet Policy: Round 1: Internet allowed, NO AI allowed. Teams must rely purely on problem statements and pseudo-code. No mobile phones or smart gadgets allowed . Round 2 & Finals: AI is completely allowed strictly for navigating files, understanding codebase layout, and analyzing system architecture —NOT for actual code solving/fixing . Raw AI prompt outputs cannot be directly copy-pasted; manual integration is mandatory due to custom package setups . Submissions & Deadlines: All modifications, reports, and final patched project repositories with a clean git commit history must be submitted within the allotted time. Strict deadlines apply . Final Deliverables: Finalists must submit a patched project repository, clean git commit history, a one-page debugging report, and present a short demo with a live Q&A session with the judges.

title: REDLINE - ARES x Google Developer Groups NSUT
organiser: Netaji Subhas University of Technology (NSUT), Delhi
description: ARES × Shunya is an AI-versus-AI Pokémon battle competition where participants develop machine-learning models or algorithmic agents to compete autonomously. These agents face off in a live, offline tournament using the Pokémon Showdown simulation engine.
eligibility: Teams of 1–2 members.
requirements: Develop and submit an autonomous AI algorithm that complies with the provided ruleset and API before the deadline.
details_text: # Event Format: Pokémon AI Battle *Society Name:* ARES Robotics x Google Developer Groups NSUT *ARES × Shunya* is an AI-versus-AI Pokémon battle competition where participants develop and submit their own machine-learning models or algorithmic agents online. The submitted AIs compete autonomously in offline, head-to-head battles using *Pokémon Showdown* as the battle simulation engine. Participants build their strategies, submit their algorithms before the deadline, and watch their AIs compete against each other in live battles. Once a battle begins, no human intervention is permitted. *Theme:* Artificial Intelligence | Robotics | Machine Learning | Strategy | Autonomous Decision-Making ## Event Details •⁠  ⁠*Team Size:* 1–2 members •⁠  ⁠*Duration:* 2.5–3 hours •⁠  ⁠*Venue:* Mini Audi •⁠  ⁠*Mode:* Online algorithm submission + offline live tournament •⁠  ⁠*Simulation Platform:* Pokémon Showdown ## Event Structure & Flow The event is conducted in two stages: online algorithm submission and an offline head-to-head tournament. ### Phase 1: Online AI Submission *Objective:* Develop an autonomous Pokémon battle AI and submit it before the competition deadline. •⁠  ⁠Participants receive the official ruleset, permitted Pokémon and moves, and the required AI interface/API. •⁠  ⁠Participants independently develop their algorithms using heuristics, probability-based strategies, decision trees, machine learning, reinforcement learning, or other permitted approaches. •⁠  ⁠Each AI must make decisions autonomously based on the battle state provided to it. •⁠  ⁠Participants may test and refine their algorithms before submission. •⁠  ⁠Submitted algorithms must comply with the competition rules and interface requirements. •⁠  ⁠Teams must submit their final AI before the announced deadline. •⁠  ⁠Submissions undergo basic validation to ensure they run correctly and return legal actions. *Important:* The submitted AI must be capable of making all in-battle decisions without human assistance. ### Phase 2: The Shunya AI Showdown — Offline Tournament *Objective:* Determine the strongest Pokémon battle AI through direct competition. •⁠  ⁠Validated participant AIs compete in head-to-head matches. •⁠  ⁠All battles use Pokémon Showdown as the simulation platform, subject to the final competition ruleset and technical integration. •⁠  ⁠Each AI autonomously chooses its moves and switches according to the information available to it. •⁠  ⁠The battle simulation resolves actions, damage, status effects, knockouts, and win conditions. •⁠  ⁠Battles are displayed live on the main screen for the audience. •⁠  ⁠A tournament bracket tracks match results and determines progression. •⁠  ⁠The final match determines the overall winner of ARES × Shunya. *Battle Flow:* 1.⁠ ⁠AI A faces AI B. 2.⁠ ⁠The simulation provides the available battle state to each AI. 3.⁠ ⁠Each AI returns its selected action. 4.⁠ ⁠Pokémon Showdown resolves the actions and updates the battle. 5.⁠ ⁠The process repeats until the match ends. 6.⁠ ⁠The result determines which AI advances in the tournament. ## Simulation Platform: Pokémon Showdown Pokémon Showdown will serve as the battle simulation platform, providing the battle mechanics and animated battle interface. The organizers will establish the permitted format, Pokémon pool, moves, and other rules before the competition. The AI integration will handle communication between participant algorithms and the simulation. The exact integration method, supported ruleset, and available battle-state information will be announced before submissions open. ## Competition Rules •⁠  ⁠Each team consists of 1–2 members. •⁠  ⁠Only submitted and validated algorithms may participate. •⁠  ⁠All participants compete under the same ruleset and simulation conditions. •⁠  ⁠No manual intervention is allowed after a match begins. •⁠  ⁠AIs must select legal actions and respond within the specified time limit. •⁠  ⁠The permitted Pokémon, moves, format, and battle mechanics

title: RAGNAROK
organiser: Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Nagpur
description: RAGNAROK is an agentic AI hackathon at IIIT Nagpur's TantraFiesta 2026 where students design and build autonomous AI systems. It features an online MCQ qualifying round followed by a 24-hour on-site building finale.
eligibility: Students currently enrolled in any college or university in India; inter-college teams are permitted.

details_text: The Agentic Hackathon | TantraFiesta 2026, IIIT Nagpur Event Detail: RAGNAROK is the flagship agentic hackathon of TantraFiesta 2026, the annual technical fest of IIIT Nagpur organized by AIRA , the AI/ML domain at CRISPR, IIIT Nagpur. The age of passive AI is ending. The next wave of software is built from agents that reason, plan, use tools, and act on their own. RAGNAROK brings together the sharpest student builders in India to design, ship, and battle-test such systems under real pressure. Qualify online. Then reach the IIIT Nagpur campus for a 24-hour build where only the best agents survive. Key Dates: Registration Deadline: 20 October, 2026 Round 1 (Online MCQ): 20 October, 2026 Round 2 (Offline Finale, IIIT Nagpur): 25th October 2026 Why You Should Participate Build something real. Work on challenging, open-ended problems that need agentic thinking, not a tutorial clone. 24 hours, one campus, India's best teams. Hack through the night with sharp peers. Surprise problem statements. Nobody knows what's coming until the finale begins. Your adaptability counts as much as your stack. Cash prizes, goodies, certificates, and recognition at one of Central India's biggest tech fests. Visibility. Your work is reviewed by experienced evaluators, and strong teams get noticed. Eligibility: Open to all students currently enrolled at any college or university in India. Inter-college and inter-university teams are allowed. There is no limit on the number of teams per college. Team Structure: Team size: 2 to 4 members. Solo participation is not allowed. One participant can be part of only one team. Every team member must register individually on Unstop. Event Format: Round 1: Online MCQ Round A timed, online objective test. It covers problem solving, AI/ML concepts, LLMs, and agentic AI concepts such as tool use, planning, memory, and prompting. The link will be shared via your registered email and the official event group. Top-scoring teams are shortlisted for the finale. Round 2: Offline Finale (IIIT Nagpur Campus) Shortlisted teams get 24 hours of continuous building on-site. Problem statements are revealed at the start of the finale. Teams build, demo, and defend their solution in front of the evaluators. Participation in the offline round is mandatory to be eligible for prizes. Rules and Guidelines: General Registration on Unstop is mandatory. Entries from unregistered participants are invalid. Decisions of the judges and organizers are final and binding. Any violation of the rules may lead to disqualification. Any public or free-to-use resource must be credited. Round 1 (Online MCQ) Tab switching is strictly not allowed. Switching tabs or windows during the test may lead to auto-submission or disqualification. The use of AI tools of any kind (chatbots, assistants, AI-powered search or solvers) is strictly prohibited. Collaboration between teams, impersonation, and any other form of malpractice will lead to disqualification. The test must be completed within the allotted time window. Round 2 (Finale) The problem statements are shared only on-site. No pre-built solutions are allowed. All development must start after the official hackathon start time. Prior code, pre-trained models, public libraries, frameworks, and APIs may be used if properly credited, but the core solution must be built during the event. Teams may use AI coding assistants and LLM APIs, since this is an agentic hackathon, but the solution must be your team's own work and you must be able to explain it fully. Plagiarism or copying another team's work leads to immediate disqualification. Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, and any required setup. Source code must be shared via a Git repository, and a working demo is required. All finalists must report to the IIIT Nagpur campus by 9:30AM on 25th October 2026. Prize Distribution: 1st Prize : 13k Cash + 12k Goodies 2nd Prize : 7k Cash + 8k Goodies 3rd Prize : 5k Cash + 5k Goodies Join the Community Joi

details_text: SYNERGY 2026: SYNERGY 2026 is an 8-Hour Hardware Simulation Hackathon organized by the Students' Council at Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering (Fr. CRCE), Bandra, Mumbai. The event brings together engineers, tinkerers, and creators to redefine sustainable product design through advanced hardware simulations. Participants will build eco-conscious, virtual prototypes without generating physical hardware waste. Tracks & Focus Areas: Electronics Domain: Design sustainable hardware solutions using virtual simulation tools such as Tinkercad, Proteus, ModelSim, or Vivado. Systems should be built around Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, or FPGA platforms, focusing on energy efficiency, minimal material use, and renewable logic. Mechanical Domain: Advance sustainable mechanical design by building CAD models and conducting simulations. Validate and optimize eco-friendly solutions using Multibody Dynamics, Motion Analysis, Finite Element Analysis (FEA), or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). Eligibility Criteria: Open to undergraduate students pursuing B.E./B.Tech, Technical Diploma, or any other UG degree. Team Size: 2 to 4 members per team. Selection & Event Timeline (1st November 2026): Screening & Allotment: Domain and problem statement lists will be provided 1 day prior to the event following registration and screening. Evaluation & Format: Two-Tier Independent Evaluation: Every team is evaluated by two separate judging panels to ensure an unbiased assessment. Round 1 is judged by Panel A, and Round 2 is independently judged by Panel B without influence from earlier scores. Aggregate Scoring: The combined score across both rounds determines final standings. Awards: Each track (Electronics and Mechanical) will have one Winner and one Runner-Up. There are no separate winners for individual problem statements. Registration Fee: Rs. 300 per team. Note: Payment is required ONLY after selection for the final offline round. Rules & Code Of Conduct: Internet access is provided at the venue; participants may refer to online resources. Mandatory carrying and displaying of official College Photo ID cards at all times on campus. Attendance is mandatory on campus for the entire 8-hour duration. Entry security screening and frisking will take place at the campus entrance. Decisions made by the judges and managing committee are final and binding. title: Tech Mafia - Trust No One. Debug Everyone.
organiser: Netaji Subhas University of Technology (NSUT), Delhi
description: Tech Mafia is a team-based social deduction game that blends technical challenges like coding and AI prompting with strategic deception. Participants must complete tasks while identifying hidden saboteurs to advance to the final individual round.
eligibility: Individual registration.
requirements: Coding, debugging, AI prompting, logical reasoning, and teamwork skills.
details_text: Tech Mafia is a team-based technical social deduction game that combines coding, debugging, AI prompting, logical reasoning, strategy, deception, and teamwork . Participants will register individually but will be assigned a team at the beginning of Round 1. They shall compete in teams of 6 , but there is a hidden conflict within every team. At the beginning of the event, each participant receives a secret role card. In every team: 4 participants are Innocents 2 participants are Mafia The Innocents must work together to complete technical challenges as efficiently as possible. The Mafia have a completely different objective: slow down, mislead, and sabotage their team without being identified. Across the first two rounds, participants must balance two things - performing well and figuring out who they can trust. At the end of Round 2, every team must identify its suspected Mafia members. The outcome of this decision determines which participants advance to the final round. Round 3 eliminates the team element completely. The remaining participants compete individually through a series of technical and mental challenges, with the Top 3 performers becoming the final winners of Tech Mafia.

details_text: What it is: AI can build an app in minutes. Proving it works is the real skill and the one that gets you hired. title: National Machine Coding, LLD and Production Debugging Contest
description: Gronex Engineering Cup #1 is a free, two-hour online contest where students and engineers solve real-world software engineering problems in a browser-based workspace. Participants tackle machine coding, low-level design, and production debugging challenges against real test suites.
eligibility: Students and working engineers.

details_text: LeetCode tests algorithms. Engineering Cup tests whether you can actually build software. Gronex Engineering Cup #1 is a free, online, 2-hour contest for students and working engineers. You solve three brand-new problems inside real code repositories, in your browser, and every submission is auto-graded against a real test suite. Platform: The contest is conducted entirely on Gronex, in its browser-based coding workspace with built-in auto-grading. Unstop is used for registration and announcements; the problems are solved and scored on Gronex at gronex.org/contest/engineering-cup-1. When: Saturday, 31 October 2026, 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM IST (2 hours, online). The Problems: Machine coding (Easy): build a working module against a real test suite. Low-level design (Hard): extend an existing codebase without breaking what already works. Production debugging (Hard): app, database and cache logs from a failing service. Find the root cause and fix the bug that took prod down. Solve in Java, Python, Node.js or C++ . Everything runs in the browser workspace, so there's nothing to install. How Scoring Works: Each problem is scored by the % of tests passing on your best run inside the contest window. Your total is the sum across the three problems (max 300). Part of each test suite is hidden and only runs at grading, so the code has to be correct, not just make the visible tests pass. Ties go to whoever reached their final total first. Run as often as you like during the contest. A live leaderboard is shown on Gronex during and after the contest. Prizes: 1st: Rs 5,000 + Gronex swag kit (bag, t-shirt, bottle) 2nd and 3rd: Gronex swag kit 4th to 10th: 1 month of Gronex Pro Everyone who submits: a verifiable certificate of participation (top performers get a Certificate of Merit) that you can add to LinkedIn How to Participate: Register here on Unstop. Register on the contest page with a verified Gronex account (free): gronex.org/contest/engineering-cup-1 At 7:00 PM IST on 31 October, the problems unlock on Gronex for registered participants. Want to warm up? Try any free problem on gronex.org. It's the same workspace and test runner you'll use on contest night. Rules: Free entry. Individual participation. One account per person; duplicate or automated accounts are disqualified. Only runs inside the contest window count. Only the AI help built into the Gronex workspace is allowed. Using outside AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) or sharing solutions during the contest is not, and may lead to disqualification after review. Swag kits ship within India; winners share a delivery address after results. Results are final after review. Gronex may disqualify entries that break these rules.

Theme: Hack. Secure. Evolve. Eligibility: Open to students pursuing B.Tech, B.E., M.Tech, M.E., BCA, MCA, B.Sc., or M.Sc. from recognized colleges and universities across India. Platform access details and VPN instructions (if required) will be shared with registered teams before the event. What to Bring (Offline Finale): Personal laptop with charger. Government-issued or college-issued photo ID for each participant. Registration confirmation (email or QR ticket) for check-in. Rules & Code of Conduct: Fair play is mandatory. Participants may attack only the systems and challenges provided within the official CTF environment. title: The Urban Autonomous Mobility Challenge by Fedex Alfa IIT Bombay
description: A national robotics competition by Techfest, IIT Bombay, where student teams design and program a scaled autonomous vehicle to navigate a miniature urban environment. The challenge tests navigation through lanes, intersections, and dynamic traffic across multiple progressive rounds.
eligibility: Undergraduate and postgraduate students from recognized institutions, organized in teams of 3-5 members.
requirements: A scaled autonomous vehicle, a 3-5 minute demonstration video, and a 1-2 page Technical Design Document (TDD).
details_text: All that you need to know about The Urban Autonomous Mobility Challenge  | Techfest 2026-27 About: The Urban Autonomous Mobility Challenge (UAMC) is a national robotics competition by Techfest, IIT Bombay, inspired by the Bosch Future Mobility Challenge, that invites student teams to design, build, and program a scaled autonomous vehicle capable of navigating a miniature urban environment entirely on its own. Teams build one vehicle that handles the complete urban circuit, lane discipline, intersections, pedestrian safety, parking, and dynamic traffic, as it escalates in complexity round by round. A remote qualification stage 6-8 weeks before the festival ensures every team arrives with a working, tested vehicle, so the 3-day festival window at Techfest, IIT Bombay, is spent proving readiness rather than debugging. Bring your self-driving car to life at Asia's largest science and technology festival. Structure: The competition runs as a remote qualification stage followed by on-site rounds, entirely within Techfest's 3-day festival window. Eligibility: Open to undergraduate/postgraduate students with a valid ID from any recognized institution. Teams may include students from different institutes. Team size: 3-5 members per team, with one designated Team Lead, fielding only one vehicle. Faculty or industry mentors may guide teams but cannot be present at or assist during any timed run. Round 1 - Qualification (Online) Teams submit a 3-5 minute video of their vehicle completing a basic lane-following and stop-at-obstacle task on a self-built practice track, along with a 1-2 page Technical Design Document (TDD) covering system architecture, perception approach, and safety design (E-stop and failure handling). Only the Team Leader may submit; multiple submissions are not accepted. The top 25 teams are invited on-site. Round 2 - On-Site Elimination Heats (Techfest, Day 1-2) Qualified teams arrive Day 1 for check-in, technical inspection, and a fixed practice slot on the actual arena. Day 2 runs two heats: the Basic Navigation Heat (lane-keeping, one stop-sign intersection, one pedestrian crossing, one static obstacle), from which the top 60% of teams advance, and the Intermediate Navigation Heat (adding a traffic-light intersection, a roundabout, and autonomous parking), from which the top 8-10 teams advance to Round 3. Round 3 - Semifinal & Grand Finale (Techfest, Day 3) The Semifinal runs the full urban circuit combining every earlier element, ranked by score, with the top 4-6 teams advancing to the Grand Finale. The Grand Finale adds a dynamic obstacle/overtaking segment and a randomized surprise rule (such as a mid-run detour) announced only at the start of the day, to test genuine generalization. Winners are determined by total score across positive points, penalties, and time-based tiebreakers, with results announced the same evening. Timeline: Registration deadline - 31st October 2026 Round 1 (Qualification) submission - 10th November 2026 Round 1 results - 17th/24th November 2026 Final arena layout released - 24th November/1st December 2026 Round 2 (Elimination Heats) - 16th-17th December 2026 Round 3 (Semifinal & Grand Finale) - 18th December 2026 Rewards And Prizes: INR 3,80,000 for the top 3 winners. Certificates for all participants who qualify for Round 2.

title: The DevForge - Hackathon

description: The Devforge is a 24-hour coding marathon where teams of 2–4 developers build innovative solutions to real-world problems. It is a high-pressure test of creativity, technical skill, and teamwork to turn concepts into working prototypes.
eligibility: College students across India; inter-college and inter-specialization teams allowed; team size 2–4 members.
requirements: Bring own laptops/chargers, submit a Round 1 technical proposal, and present a working prototype.
details_text: “Exploit the Code. Forge the Future.” Description: The Devforge is a 24-hour coding marathon where teams of 2–4 developers brainstorm, design, and build innovative solutions to real-world problems under pressure. Collaborate with your squad, tackle challenges, and race against the clock as you turn bold ideas from concept into working solutions — a true test of creativity, problem-solving, teamwork, and technical skill . Eligibility: Open to college students across India Inter-college teams are allowed Inter-specialization teams are allowed Team size must be between 2 to 4 members Rules & Regulations: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, and devices. Internet access will be provided. Pre-built projects are not allowed. All code must be written during the hackathon (libraries/frameworks permitted). Teams must present a working prototype at the end. Participants are required to stay on campus for the duration of the hackathon(Food will be provided in the campus) Teams must adhere to all guidelines and submission formats The judges’ decision will be final. Code Freeze: Submission deadline for Day 1 code freeze (09:00 AM) is absolute; no further commits will be considered for Round 2 evaluation. Registration Process: Note: The hackathon will consist of 2 rounds . Problem statements of the hackathon will be released during the Round 1 registration period. Participants must select one of the provided problem statements and base their Round 1 submission on the selected problem statement. The Round 1 submission must demonstrate how the team intends to approach and solve the selected problem statement . Shortlisted teams will proceed to the 24-hour offline hackathon at the Scaler School of Technology (SST) campus. The final shortlisted teams will compete in the Grand Stage Finals through live presentations and working product demonstrations. Round 1: Register online with team details through Unstop. Select one problem statement from the problem statements released for Round 1. Submit a Plain-text / Markdown / PDF document addressing the selected problem statement and covering: Proposed System Architecture Technical Implementation Strategy Chosen Tech Stack & Tooling Anticipated Challenges & Risk Mitigation Expected Deliverables Presentations/PPTs are not accepted for Round 1. Teams will be evaluated based on the quality, technical depth, feasibility, and clarity of their proposed solution to the selected problem statement . Selected teams will be notified on the registered email. Round 2 (Final Round): Round 2 will be held completely offline on campus premises. Teams will develop their projects in a collaborative, energized environment, with access to mentorship, high-speed internet, and refreshments. Participants are advised to reach the venue 1 hour before the commencement time. This will be a 24 hour event (overnight hackathon). Teams will develop their solutions and undergo desk-side judging on Day 1 morning , including a PPT walkthrough, live functional prototype demo, and codebase analysis. The Top 10 teams will qualify as finalists Finalist teams will present their solutions and working prototypes before the judges, and the final results will be based on these presentations and evaluations . Disqualification Criteria: Plagiarism or code copying Submitting incomplete or non-functional prototypes Submitting pre-existing projects, cloning repositories without substantial original contributions, or fabricating Git history. Misconduct, offensive behavior, or disrupting the event flow Presenting mockups or pre-rendered videos as live working software during evaluation. Any form of harassment, destruction of venue facilities, or failure to follow event organizers and campus security directives. title: Vihaan X: Software Track

details_text: About the Competition Vihaan X is North India's largest student-run hackathon, organised by IEEE DTU. The Software Track is a celebration of innovation through code, where participants collaborate to build impactful digital solutions in an intense 24-hour window. The format is structured as 8 hours of coding, 8 hours of building, and 8 hours of debugging — pushing teams to turn ideas into fully functional applications. From AI-powered platforms and full-stack web apps to mobile and system-level solutions, this track is where ambitious builders ship real products, not just prototypes. Teams design scalable, user-centric solutions while getting mentored by industry experts throughout the event. Software Track Domains HealthTech FinTech Education Web3 & Blockchain E-Sports Women's Safety Security Sustainability Open Innovation Team Size Maximum of 4 participants per team. Rounds: Day 1: Building and developing projects, from core features to a working prototype Day 2 (around 10 AM): Project evaluation and judging Final Round: Shortlisted teams present to industry experts Winners are announced after final presentations Learning Opportunities Direct mentorship from industry experts throughout the event Exposure to modern tools, frameworks, and development practices Hands-on experience building real-world software solutions from scratch Rewards & Opportunity Exciting cash prizes and exclusive rewards for winning teams Recognition for the most innovative and impactful solutions A collaborative environment that fuels creativity, learning, and execution — 24 hours to code, build, and ship something that matters Venue: Delhi Technological University WhatsApp Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/LhXp4DQOVgEIP6yxeeY37V

title: Drone Soccer | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A drone soccer competition where teams pilot custom-built, caged drones through an obstacle-filled arena to score points by flying through a circular goal ring. Matches are conducted as timed sprints focusing on agility, defense, and scoring precision.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 5 members; cross-college teams are allowed.
requirements: Custom-built or configured drones with protective cages (no standard RTF models) and the use of only one main drone model.
details_text: Rules & Guidelines: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members . Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up. Model Regulations: Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited. Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted. Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches. Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited. A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls. Event Structure: Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown: Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones. Goal Scoring Task: Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points. Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution. If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run. Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

title: Multirotor | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: A two-round drone competition where teams navigate through rings and obstacles to complete a payload delivery task. Participants must fly custom-built drones to score points through precision maneuvering and QR code identification.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 members; inter-college teams are permitted.
requirements: A custom-built drone (no RTF models) equipped with an onboard camera for QR scanning.
details_text: Rules: Team Structure: Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 6 members. Participants from different colleges can form a team. Model Regulations: Each team must have its own custom-built drone; exchanging models between teams is strictly prohibited. RTF (Ready-To-Fly) models are not allowed, but pre-programmed boards can be used. Only one model can be used throughout all competition rounds. Flight and Conduct Rules: No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams can have a 2-minute trial before Round 2. Lifting the drone manually to improve position during any round is not allowed. Any failed landing attempt that does not result in a score immediately ends the round. The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on any disputes. Event Structure: Round 1: Teams must fly their drone through 5 circular rings placed at varying heights (between 1 meter to 2.5 meters). Each ring carries different points based on difficulty. Teams must avoid touching the rings to earn points. Skipping a ring results in no points but does not incur a penalty. Maximum time for completion: 8 minutes. Qualification Criteria: Teams with the highest scores will advance to Round 2. Round 2: Obstacle Navigation: Teams must maneuver through multiple obstacles, which will be disclosed on the spot. Payload Task: The onboard camera scans a QR code to identify a specific payload. If scanning fails, teams can receive the QR details manually but will lose detection points. The identified payload must be dropped into a designated area. No penalty for unsuccessful drops, but no points are awarded either.

title: Beat The Market | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: This two-round competition challenges participants to build a stock portfolio based on financial analysis and subsequently develop a machine learning model to predict the future prices of those selected stocks.
eligibility: UG and PG college students; teams of up to 5 members.
requirements: Team formation, portfolio construction with financial justification, and machine learning model development.
details_text: Event Structure: Online Round: Portfolio Building & Analysis: All registered teams will receive details of 20 virtual stocks, including their technical and fundamental analysis. Participants must study the stocks and create a portfolio of 8 stocks using a virtual fund of ₹20 lakh. Teams must present a rationale for their selection, supported by financial statements, news articles, or relevant market data. Bonus Challenge: Justify why the remaining 12 stocks were excluded from your portfolio. ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors may be incorporated into the portfolio for additional evaluation. Portfolios will be assessed based on stock performance two years into the future, assuming the investments were made in the current year. Offline Round: Machine Learning-Based Stock Price Prediction: Teams will create a Machine Learning model to predict stock prices for each of the 8 selected stocks in their portfolio. A time series model can be used to forecast future price movements. Historical stock data (till Dec 2024) will be provided for training the model. The model will be evaluated on stock prices from 2025-2026. The team with the best-performing model will win the competition. A bonus round will be held, with further details provided on campus. Guidelines: Team Composition & Registration: Each team can have up to 5 members (both UG and PG students are eligible). A participant cannot be part of multiple teams in the same event. Multiple teams from the same college are allowed to participate. Competition & Evaluation: Only college students will be considered when deciding the winners. Teams must justify their portfolio selections with supporting financial data. Machine Learning models will be tested on real stock data from 2025-2026. Rules & Fair Play: The decision of the judges is final and incontestable. The organizers reserve the right to modify the timeline if necessary.

title: Techkriti Grand Prix | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR

eligibility: Students (inter-college teams allowed, maximum 6 members per team).
requirements: Custom-built Nitro or Electric RC car, valid student ID, and all necessary supplies such as fuel and batteries.
details_text: Introduction: Welcome to Techkriti Grand Prix ‘27, the ultimate RC car competition! Build your RC car from scratch, combining engineering, design, and coding expertise. It’s not just about speed—precision, control, and strategy will set you apart. Test your skills on a challenging track where every decision matters. Showcase your innovation as you race head-to-head with other competitors. This event pushes the limits of creativity and engineering, offering an exciting experience filled with competition and learning. Are you ready to take the green light and race toward glory? General Rules: Each team can have a maximum of 6 members. The students must carry valid student ID cards from their college. The car has 2 categories: Nitro and electric. A team may consist of students from different colleges. Certificates of Excellence will be awarded to the top three teams. Teams must bring fuel, batteries, etc. Nothing will be provided by the organizers. The name of your car should be clearly mentioned on it. The arena shown is just for reference. It may be different from what is shown here, but the tasks will remain the same. The organizers reserve the right to change the rules as they deem fit. The judge's decision will be the final decision. Change in rules, if any, will be highlighted on the website and notified to the registered teams on prior notice.

title: IARC | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: This flagship Techkriti event challenges participants to design, build, and program an autonomous robot from scratch to perform specific tasks. Robots are judged on their precision, fabrication, and the intelligent application of sensors and coding.
eligibility: Teams of up to 6 students, including inter-college teams.
requirements: Build an autonomous robot from scratch capable of performing tasks using sensors and code.
details_text: Introduction: This event is about an autonomous robot built by the participants from scratch. The robot is judged based on its ability to perform usual tasks. The event considers the precision level in the design and fabrication of the bot and the intelligent use of sensors and coding. This is one of the flagship events of Techkriti, witnessing large participation from across the country and also around the globe. It saw the participation of 40+ teams in the final round last time. General Rules: Each team can have a maximum of 6 participants. A team may consist of students from different colleges. Certificates of Excellence will be awarded to the top three teams. Bots should not be disassembled until the results are declared. When a team is called for a match, they must report within five minutes. The arena shown is just for reference. It may be different from what is shown here, but the tasks will remain the same. The organizers reserve the right to change the rules as they deem fit. The judge's decision will be the final decision. Changes in rules, if any, will be highlighted on the website and notified to the registered teams on prior notice.

title: Manoeuvre | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
description: Design and build a manually controlled robot capable of precisely gripping various shapes and inserting them into corresponding grooves on a cubic block.
eligibility: Teams of 2 to 6 students, including inter-college teams.
requirements: A custom-built robot with a precise gripping mechanism and a stable wired or wireless control system.
details_text: Task: Bot Design: The bot must be manually controlled and capable of gripping various blocks or shapes. It should be able to insert them into corresponding grooves carved into a cubic block. The gripping mechanism should be precise and able to handle various shapes securely. Control Mechanism: The bot can be either wired or wireless. If wired, the cable should be long enough to ensure it remains slack and does not interfere with the bot’s movement. Wireless control options include a dual-frequency remote, Bluetooth, or Wi-Fi. Task Precision: The bot should be able to precisely align and place the blocks into their respective grooves, requiring accurate control of its movements and gripping mechanism. Flexibility and Range: For wireless bots, ensure the control mechanism provides a stable connection and sufficient range to operate effectively within the task area without any interference or lag. Rules and Regulations: Each team can have a maximum of 6 participants and a minimum of 2 A team may consist of students from different colleges. Teams have to make their robot. They can't use the other team's robot. Certificates of Excellence will be awarded to the top three teams. Judges/organizers' decision will be final.

title: Craft N Code (West Bengal)
organiser: International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Bhubaneswar
description: Craft N Code is a state-level hackathon organized by Jadavpur University where students showcase innovation and coding skills to qualify for the national round. It provides a platform for students to develop technology-driven solutions for real-world problems.
eligibility: Students studying in colleges located within West Bengal.
requirements: Develop and present a technical solution in tracks such as HealthTech, EdTech, Cybersecurity, Mobility, AgriTech, or Open Innovation.
details_text: Craft N Code – West Bengal State Qualifier This State Round is exclusively for students studying in colleges across West Bengal. Please register only if your institution is located in West Bengal. Get ready to showcase your innovation, creativity, and coding skills at the Craft N Code West Bengal State Qualifier, organized by Jadavpur University. This qualifier provides an opportunity for West Bengal's talented student innovators to showcase their skills and compete for a chance to advance to the Craft N Code National Hackathon, hosted by IIIT Bhubaneswar. The West Bengal State Qualifier will follow a structured evaluation process where teams will get the opportunity to understand the challenge, brainstorm innovative ideas, develop technology-driven solutions, and present their projects. Participants will be evaluated on their problem-solving approach, innovation, technical implementation, creativity, presentation, and overall impact of their solutions. Important Dates: Registration Opens: 29 August 2026 Submission Window: 1 September 2026–30 October 2026 Craft N Code is more than just a coding competition, it is a platform for solving real-world problems through technology, collaboration, creativity, and innovation. Participants will get the opportunity to transform their ideas into practical solutions while working alongside talented students and developers from across West Bengal. The following are the tracks for the prelims: HealthTech: Build solutions that improve access, quality, or efficiency of healthcare. Think about diagnostics, telemedicine platforms, mental health tools, patient record management, wearable-driven health monitoring, etc. EdTech: Create tools that make learning more personalized, accessible, or effective. This spans adaptive learning platforms, skill-gap assessment tools, accessibility aids for differently-abled learners, solutions for low-resource/rural education, etc. Cybersecurity & Privacy: Tackle problems around securing systems, data, and identities. Ideas can include threat/anomaly detection, secure authentication mechanisms, privacy-preserving data sharing, tools that help everyday users protect themselves online, etc. Mobility & Transportation: Solve for movement of people or goods; traffic optimization, EV charging infrastructure, public transit efficiency, logistics/fleet management, road safety, etc. AgriTech & Food Security: Address challenges across the farm-to-table chain: crop health monitoring, yield prediction, supply chain traceability, market access for farmers, food waste reduction, etc. Open Innovation: No fixed domain - bring any technically sound idea that solves a genuine problem, even outside the five tracks above. This is the track for interdisciplinary or unconventional ideas. If you're ready to challenge yourself, build innovative solutions, and showcase your technical skills, this is your opportunity to step forward. Let's innovate. Let's build. Let's Craft N Code.

title: Prompt Battle

description: Prompt Battle is a fast-paced AI-powered development and prompt-engineering competition where participants build functional solutions using Generative AI tools. The event features surprise hurdles and concludes with a live showcase and judge Q&A.

details_text: Prompt Battle is a fast-paced AI-powered development and prompt-engineering competition where participants receive a problem statement and build a functional solution using Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools. title: Triathlon
organiser: M.S. Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences
description: Triathlon is a three-round interconnected technical competition featuring coding quizzes, PC building challenges, and cybersecurity puzzles. Performance in each round provides resources or hints for the subsequent round, rewarding consistent skill across all three disciplines.
eligibility: Teams of 2–3 members.
requirements: Knowledge of programming, computer science, PC hardware, and cybersecurity.
details_text: About the Event Welcome to Triathlon — a three-round technical event run as one connected game. Unlike a normal multi-round event, the rounds are linked: what a team earns in one round becomes a resource it spends in the next, so consistency across all three rounds decides the winner. There is no elimination — every team plays all three rounds and the scores are added up to find the ultimate champion! Event Format & Process Team Size: 2–3 members per team. Round 1: Coding & CS Quiz (25 min): A timed quiz on programming and computer science fundamentals, including 'predict the output', 'find the bug', and spotting a hidden mistake in AI-written code. The top 4 teams will play a live buzzer round. Reward: Your Round 1 score sets your team's budget for Round 2. Round 2: PC Build Fix & Adapt (60 min): Teams are given a faulty PC parts list on PCPartPicker and must find and fix the mistakes. Midway through, the requirements change (budget or use-case) and teams must rework the build and briefly justify their choices. Reward: Your Round 2 score converts into hint points for Round 3. Round 3: CTF Puzzle Hunt (50 min): A Jeopardy-style set of cybersecurity puzzles including hidden messages, simple ciphers, web and forensics challenges. One special clue is even hidden on a poster in the CSE block! Hint points earned in Round 2 can be spent here. Rules Teams must consist of exactly 2 to 3 members. No Elimination: All teams will participate in all three rounds. Scoring: The team with the highest combined score across all three rounds wins. Tie-Breaker: In the event of a tie, the team that completed Round 3 in the shortest amount of time will be declared the winner. Anti-Cheat (Round 3): Each team gets team-specific flags so answers cannot be shared. A live scoreboard will be projected during this round.

title: Zero Hour
organiser: M S Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences
description: Zero Hour is an intense, 3-hour hackathon that tests coding, adaptability, and teamwork through surprise challenges. Teams must build a technical solution while navigating unexpected 'Gauntlets' to see if they can survive the clock.
eligibility: Teams of exactly 4 members.
requirements: Build a technical solution within 3 hours and ensure at least 3 different members participate in the timed Gauntlet challenges.
details_text: About the Event Think a hackathon is just pick a problem, open your laptop, and start coding? Think again. Welcome to Zero Hour — a hackathon where coding is only part of the game. You will have to code, adapt, communicate, make quick decisions, and keep your team moving when things stop going according to plan. The question is simple: When the clock hits zero, will your team have what it takes to survive? Event Format & Process Duration: 3 hours of intense building and adapting. Team Size: 4 members per team. Kickoff: Teams will choose a mystery theme and race to build a working technical solution before time runs out. The Gauntlets: Just when you find your rhythm, 3 surprise challenges will be introduced. These are assigned to 3 different team members. Every Gauntlet is timed, every point matters, and your team’s final score depends on how well each member performs during their turn. The Final Push: Submit your solution, face the judges, and defend what you built. Rules Teams must consist of exactly 4 members. No hiding behind the strongest coder—at least 3 different team members must participate in the Gauntlet challenges. Solutions must be built within the 3-hour timeframe; no extra time will be provided.

title: Respawn
organiser: M S Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences
description: RESPAWN is a 2D game jam where teams build a themed game during a 12-hour online prototyping phase. Shortlisted teams then move to an offline live pitching and showcase event to present their final playable games to a panel of judges.
eligibility: Teams of 3–4 members.
requirements: Develop a 2D game based on a specific theme, submit three progress videos at 4-hour intervals, and attend the offline live pitching session.
details_text: Welcome to the Rspawn - by M S Ramaiah University of Applied Sciences! About the Opportunity: RESPAWN – The 2D Game Jam is your chance to build it, play it and bring it to life! Participants will be added to an official WhatsApp group after registration and the general theme will be revealed at 9AM on October 13, marking the start of the 12-Hour Online Building Round from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Teams of 3–4 members can bring their ideas to life by building their own 2D game based on the given theme in any genre, using any game engine or framework of their choice. The Google Drive link for submitting their 3 screen-recorded progress videos at 4-hour intervals will be shared in the group along with further instructions. Simple creative elements such as patterns, symmetry or other mathematical touches can also be incorporated for additional points. After the 12-hour building round, teams will get 2 days (October 14 and 15) to polish their games, fix bugs, improve gameplay and get their final builds ready. The offline round will be on October 16 with a Live Pitching & Showcase, where teams will showcase their final playable games on campus before the judges, where each team will have 5 minutes to present their game, followed by 3 minutes for Q&A about their game and its technical implementation. Teams will be evaluated based on the submitted videos, documentation, creativity, technical execution, gameplay, and presentation, with the best teams competing to claim the title of RESPAWN Champion! Competition Structure: Day 1 (12-Hour Online Rapid Prototyping Phase): Conducted fully online prior to the campus event. Teams get 12 continuous hours tc build their 2D game. The use of boilerplate code, game templates, pre-designed sprites, or a near-complete engine starter kit prepared beforehand is allowed, but to prevent teams from providing an already pre-developed game, the official 2D game theme will be released in the official WhatsApp group immediately after registrations close, and the game must be developed strictly based on that theme. To track real-time progress, teams must submit 3 screen-recorded progress videos (one every 4 hours showing the current build status) via a dedicated Google Drive submission link. Each progress video must clearly display the date and time of the recording within the video itself. Intermission: 1-day break for rest, final bug-fixing, and preparation for the live showcase. Day 2 (3-Hour Offline Live Pitching & Showcase): Held on campus. All shortlisted teams from Day 1 must bring their completed playable games to present live before a panel of industry judges. Failure to attend will result in disqualification. Each team gets a 7-minute pitch slot (4-minute live gameplay demo + pitch, 3-minute judge Q&A). Judges evaluate final game stability, mechanical complexity, artwork/sound, and adherence to the mathematical aesthetic criteria.
