title: Dohyo: Robo Sumo
organiser: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology (GTBIT), New Delhi
description: Dohyo is a head-to-head robotic pushing competition where two remotely controlled robots battle to push their opponent out of a circular arena or immobilize them. The event tests power, traction, and strategy through intense knockout-style matches.
eligibility: Open to all students, including inter-college participants.
requirements: Teams of 3–5 members must provide a wireless-controlled robot (max 8kg, 30x40x30 cm, 48V DC) equipped with a mandatory emergency stop switch.
details_text: Dohyo is a head-to-head robotic pushing competition that puts power, traction, control, and strategy to the test. Two remotely controlled robots face off in a circular arena, with the objective of pushing the opponent completely outside the boundary or immobilising it. With intense 2-minute matches and knockout rounds, every push, manoeuvre, and positioning decision can determine the winner. "Push. Outsmart. Dominate." Details: Category: Power Duration: 2 Hours Date: 17th October 2026 Time: 12:30 PM onwards Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology Mode: Offline Team Size: 3–5 participants Eligibility Criteria: Open to all students. Inter-college participants allowed. Pre-requisites: Competition-ready wireless-controlled robot complying with the specifications below: Maximum weight: 8 kg Maximum dimensions: 30 × 40 × 30 cm Maximum voltage: 48V DC Control: Wireless only Operator: Single operator per match Wired control: Not permitted Emergency Stop/Kill Switch: Mandatory Event Flow: Each match will have a maximum duration of 2 minutes . A match ends immediately if a robot is completely pushed outside the arena. A robot may also win if the opponent becomes immobilised , defined as no wheel rotation for approximately 10 seconds . If neither robot wins within the time limit, the judges will determine the result based on the applicable tie-break criteria. For fewer than 7 teams , a Round Robin stage will be conducted, followed by the top 4 teams qualifying for the knockout stage. For 7–10 teams , teams will be divided into 2 groups , with the top 2 teams from each group qualifying for the knockout stage. In the knockout stage: Semifinal 1: Rank 1 vs Rank 4 Semifinal 2: Rank 2 vs Rank 3 Final: Winners of the semifinals In the group stage, points will be awarded as: Win: 3 points Draw: 1 point each Loss: 0 points Teams will be given 2 minutes of pit/repair time between rounds. A tiebreaker match will be conducted if required to determine qualification or final standings. Rules & Regulations: The robot must comply with the specified 8 kg weight, 30 × 40 × 30 cm dimensions, and 48V DC maximum voltage limits. Only wireless control is permitted. Wired control of the robot is strictly prohibited. Only one operator is permitted to control the robot during a match. Weapons, projectiles, explosives, pyrotechnics, flammable substances, high-pressure systems, or any mechanism designed to damage another robot or person are strictly prohibited. The arena will be a circular platform with a diameter of 160 cm , featuring a clearly visible boundary and a flat, stable surface. Robots must begin from their designated starting positions, approximately 20–30 cm apart , and must remain stationary until the official start signal. Both robots must be fully inside the arena before the match begins. Each robot must be equipped with a functional Emergency Stop/Kill Switch . Any intentional interference with another team's wireless control system is strictly prohibited. Robots will undergo weigh-in and verification before competition. Re-verification may be required after any in-competition repair or modification. A robot pushed completely outside the arena boundary will be declared defeated. A robot showing no wheel rotation for approximately 10 seconds may be declared immobilised and defeated. Any unsafe operation or violation of the rules may result in a warning, penalty, or disqualification at the discretion of the event officials. The decision of the event judges and marshals regarding match results, penalties, and disqualifications will be considered final.

eligibility: Open to all students, including inter-college participants.

details_text: Takeshi's Bots is a fully autonomous maze-navigation challenge that tests a robot's accuracy, sensing, path planning, and decision-making. Robots must independently navigate a covered 3 × 3 m maze, overcome dead ends, and reach the centrally located finish without any human or remote intervention. Details: Category: Accuracy(fully autonomous) Duration: 2 Hours Date: 17th October 2026 Time : 12:00 PM Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology Mode: Offline Team Size: 3-5 participants No. of rounds: 3 attempts per team (best valid time to be considered) Eligibility Criteria: Open to all students Inter-college participants allowed. Pre-requisites: Competition-ready robot complying with the specs below: 20x20x15 cm, max 48V DC, fully autonomous — no remote/human control during official run (only onboard sensing: ultrasonic, IR, ToF, LiDAR, cameras, encoders, IMU, etc.) Event Flow: 3 attempts per team, max 5 minutes per attempt; best valid completion time counts Failure to reach FINISH within 5 minutes = DNF Tie-breaker: one-on-one additional run, lower valid time wins Organisers install an external monitoring device (min. 8x8 cm mounting area) on each robot before every attempt. Rules & Regulations: Arena: square 300x300 cm, 25 cm outer wall height, 35 cm corridor width, covered from top; FINISH at centre. No inspecting/photographing/recording the maze before or during the official attempt Slight/incidental wall contact allowed; forceful/repeated contact altering the maze layout = violation, may DQ the attempt DQ if robot knocks down a wall, breaks maze sections, opens an unintended route, or damages the maze Deliberate human intervention during a run → DQ; robot simply failing on its own → DNF Teams must not obstruct, modify, disconnect, or interfere with the organiser's monitoring device

title: Overdrive: Robo Race
organiser: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology (GTBIT), New Delhi
description: Overdrive is a high-speed wireless rover racing challenge where teams compete to navigate a Melbourne F1-style track in the shortest time. Participants must balance aggressive driving with precision to conquer obstacles like ramps, rollers, and gravel pits.
eligibility: Open to all students, including inter-college participants.
requirements: Teams of 3–5 members with a wireless-controlled rover (max 2kg, 8x8x8 inches, 48V DC) and a front-mounted white LED.
details_text: Overdrive is a high-speed wireless rover racing challenge that tests speed, precision, control, and driving skills. Teams compete to complete a Melbourne F1-style track featuring ramps, rollers, gravel pits, and airborne sections in the shortest possible time. With 3 laps per attempt and 2 attempts per team, racers must balance aggressive driving with precision while avoiding penalties. The fastest valid run conquers the track. "Accelerate. Control. Conquer." Details: Category: Speed Duration: 2 Hours Date: 17th October 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology Mode: Offline Team Size: 3–5 participants No. of rounds: 2 attempts per team (3 laps per attempt; best valid attempt considered) Eligibility Criteria: Open to all students. Inter-college participants allowed. Pre-requisites: Competition-ready wireless-controlled rover complying with the specifications below: Maximum weight: 2 kg Maximum dimensions: 8 × 8 × 8 inches Maximum voltage: 48V DC Control: Wireless only — Wi-Fi, BLE, RF, LoRa, nRF24L01, or commercial RC systems Operator: Single operator per run Wired control: Not permitted Event Flow: One rover will be allowed on the track at a time. Each team gets 2 attempts , with 3 laps per attempt . Each attempt has a maximum time limit of 5 minutes . Checkpoint detection will be performed using a front-mounted white LED and LDR-based checkpoint system . The Final Time = Race Time + Penalty Time . The team with the lowest valid Final Time will rank highest. Tie-breaker: lower penalty time will be considered first; if still tied, the better time from the team's other attempt will be considered. Failure to complete all 3 laps within the time limit will result in DNF . Rules & Regulations: The rover must comply with the specified 2 kg weight, 8-inch maximum dimensions, and 48V DC maximum voltage limits. Only wireless control is permitted. Wired control of the rover is strictly prohibited. Each rover must have a front-mounted white LED that remains visible to the checkpoint detection system throughout the run. Only one operator is permitted to control the rover during an attempt. Weapons, projectiles, explosives, pyrotechnics, flammable substances, high-pressure systems, or any mechanism designed to damage another rover or person are strictly prohibited. Any form of jamming or intentional signal interference with another team's rover is prohibited. Knocking a boundary or obstacle will incur a +3 second penalty . An off-track excursion will incur a +5 second penalty . A manual reset will incur a +10 second penalty . Missing a checkpoint will result in lap invalidation or a +20 second penalty , as determined by the organisers. Unsafe or reckless driving may result in a warning and, if repeated or severe, disqualification . A rover that fails to complete all 3 laps within the 5-minute limit will be marked DNF .

title: Junior Robo Soccer
description: Junior Robo Soccer at TechTrix'26 is a robotics competition where teams use wirelessly controlled robots to compete in football-style matches. The objective is to maneuver a ball into the opponent's goal while adhering to specific technical and gameplay constraints.
eligibility: Teams of 2 participants.
requirements: A custom-built wireless robot (max 350x350mm, 3kg, 12V DC), a controller, necessary spares, and a ₹300 registration fee per team.
details_text: Event Details Date: 23 October 2026 Time: 4:00 PM – 5:30 PM Venue: Basketball Court, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida Registration Fee: ₹300 per team Prize Pool: ₹12,000 Team Size: 2 participants per team Coordinator: Ms. Diksha Singh Event Description Welcome to Junior Robo Soccer at TechTrix'26, where robotics meets the excitement of football! Teams compete head-to-head using a custom-built, wirelessly controlled robot to maneuver a ball into the opponent's goal. Each team fields only one robot in the arena during a match. Control your robot, defend your goal, outplay your opponent, and score by getting the ball completely across the goal line. Guidelines Team & Robot Specifications Team Size: 2 participants per team Maximum Dimensions: 350 × 350 mm (L × W) Maximum Weight: 3 kg, including chassis, kicking mechanism, and batteries Maximum Voltage: 3S LiPo, 12V  DC/3s (fully charged) — IC engines, pneumatics, and compressors prohibited Control: Fully wireless (RF or Bluetooth) manual control — no wired tethers, autonomous operation strictly banned Ball Handling: at least 50% of the ball's surface must remain exposed at all times — mechanisms that fully trap, grab, suction, or swallow the ball are prohibited Participants must bring their own robot, controller, and necessary spares Pre-Event Inspection Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time Every robot undergoes a technical inspection and weigh-in; robots failing weight, dimension, power, or ball-handling checks will be disqualified before the match begins Arena & Match Format Arena: 8 ft × 4 ft, with 60 cm wide goal posts on each side Single-elimination knockout format, with byes (for uneven team counts) assigned via random draw A standard match consists of 2 rounds of up to 90 seconds each; the ball starts at centre with robots inside their defence "D" until the referee's signal A goal is scored when the ball completely crosses the goal line; a round is won by the first team to score, or tied if no goal is scored in 90 seconds A team wins the match by winning both rounds, or winning one and tying the other 30-second break between rounds, with teams switching sides If the ball goes out of bounds, play pauses, robots freeze in place, and the ball resets to centre A robot that completely stops working mid-round causes an automatic round forfeit for that team (it may still play the next round if repaired during the break) An unsafe or uncontrollable robot may be removed from the match by the referee, who may also stop play for safety, ball recovery, or technical reasons Tie-Breaker If tied after 2 rounds, a 3rd Tie-Breaker Round (max 90 seconds, first goal wins) is played If the 3rd round also ends 0-0, the winner is the team with the fewest accumulated penalties across all three rounds If goals and penalties are completely tied, judges decide based on Aggression and Control Judging Criteria Penalties are tallied (not awarded as free kicks) and used as a tie-breaker: Stalling (5-second rule): holding/pinning/trapping the ball in one position for over 5 seconds — 1 penalty point Goal camping (5-second rule): parking entirely inside your own goal for over 5 seconds without playing the ball — 1 penalty point Wall pinning (5-second rule): pinning the opponent against the arena wall while fighting for the ball for over 5 seconds — 1 penalty point Aggressive ramming: intentionally and repeatedly ramming the opponent instead of playing the ball — 1 penalty point Hand touches: manually resetting a flipped/stuck robot — 1 penalty point each Disqualification The following will result in disqualification: Exceeding the published dimensions, weight, or voltage limits Using a wired controller or autonomous operation Ball-trapping/suction mechanisms that leave less than 50% of the ball exposed Deliberately damaging another team's robot Receiving unauthorized external assistance Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul/abusive language, or intent

Hand-Touch Penalty: +15 seconds per touch (maximum 3 per race). Obstacle-Skip Penalty: +20 seconds per skipped obstacle (maximum 2 per race). Disqualification: A team may be disqualified for: Exceeding the specified dimensions, weight, or power limit. Deliberate or reckless damage to the venue, track, or equipment. The decision of the judges and organising committee is final and binding regarding performance, penalties, disqualification, and competition-related disputes. details_text: Note: Mandatory Registration on : https://techfest.org/workshops/prompt-engineering All further updates will be  from Techfest website only ,its mandatory to register in the website . All that you need to know about Techfest Prompt Engineering Workshop Prompt Engineering Workshop: Prompt Engineering is the practice of turning a raw AI model into a precise, reliable tool  structuring instructions well enough to get accurate, consistent, and usable output every single time. It sits at the intersection of human intent and AI systems, going far beyond "how to talk to ChatGPT" to cover grounding prompts in real data, multimodal inputs, and prompt security  the exact standards enterprise AI teams work with in 2026. Today, this skill is being demanded across every function, not just tech roles: software, finance, healthcare, marketing, legal, and education are all pairing domain expertise with the ability to drive AI effectively, a combination that pays a premium over either skill alone. From building multi-step reasoning chains to structuring content so AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude actually cite it (Generative Engine Optimization, the AI-era equivalent of SEO), businesses now run on well-engineered prompts, not lucky guesses  and this workshop teaches you to build them. Across two intensive offline days at IIT Bombay, you'll go from foundational prompt structures to a real, evaluated prompt system you'll design, test, and refine yourself  no prior AI or coding background required. Workshop Content Foundations of Prompt Engineering Prompt Structuring & Response Shaping Context, Memory & RAG Domain-Specific & Multimodal Prompting Zero-Shot & Few-Shot Learning Advanced Prompting: Chaining & Reasoning Patterns Adaptive & Self-Optimizing Prompt Systems Prompt Security & Evaluation AI Search & GEO Capstone: Build & Test Systems + Certification

description: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline…
details_text: Event Title: 2-Day Offline Workshop on Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems Registration: Complete the process at https://techfest.org/workshops/agentic-ai Venue & Format: Lecture Hall Complex, IIT Bombay Campus | Offline (Concept Sessions, Live Demos & Hands-On Practice) Limited Seat available: About the Workshop Agentic AI represents the biggest paradigm shift in applied artificial intelligence since basic chatbots. Modern enterprise solutions are rapidly evolving from simple single-turn systems to fully autonomous, tool-using agents capable of planning, deciding, and acting. This intensive 2-day hands-on workshop covers the entire agent lifecycle—from core reasoning loops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to multi-agent orchestration, safety guardrails, and real-world deployment. Participants will build functional agents from scratch using industry-standard frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Why You Should Attend: Master Next-Gen Tech: Deep-dive into the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—the open standard for connecting models directly to enterprise tools and data. Hands-On Experience: Build, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end agents with real-world execution. Framework Mastery: Gain direct technical exposure to LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and vector database integrations. Production-Grade Design: Learn memory management, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) checkpoints, system safety, and token-cost optimization. Workshop Syllabus & Core Topics: Agentic Foundations & Architectures: Transition from chatbots to autonomous agents, master the Sense-Think-Act-Reflect loop, explore operational autonomy levels, and identify failure mitigation strategies. LLM Integration & Prompting: Optimize context windows, implement function calling with JSON schema structured outputs, design production-grade system prompts, and analyze model speed/cost trade-offs. Reasoning & Planning Patterns: Implement multi-step reasoning patterns including ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree-of-Thought alongside automated task decomposition and Orchestrator-Worker routes. Tool Execution & Safety Checkpoints: Design robust tool schemas for deterministic APIs, handle errors with auto-retries, optimize execution (parallel vs. sequential), and integrate Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) safety checks. Model Context Protocol (MCP): Build, connect, and sandbox custom MCP servers using standard Host/Client/Server architecture, primitives, and transport mechanisms (stdio vs. HTTP/SSE). Memory Management & RAG Pipelines: Architect dynamic short-term context and persistent long-term memory using vector databases, context engineering, dynamic session state, and high-retrieval RAG. Multi-Agent Systems & Frameworks: Construct peer-to-peer and hierarchical agent topologies using state handoffs, while comparing leading frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Capstone Build & Deployment: Hands-on experience building, debugging, benchmarking, and applying guardrails to deploy a production agent as an API, Web App, or Chat Interface.

details_text: Introduction: The case teaching method has become a way of teaching in B-Schools across the globe, providing students with real-time experience. The Management Case Conference (MCC) is an endeavour to motivate academicians, practitioners, consultants, and research scholars to come up with the best solution to a business situation. The case conference aims to encourage and promote the development of high-quality cases of both national and international relevance. Participants from all over the world are invited to participate and share their experiences. This year will be the 5th edition of MCC. It will be held on November 6, 2026. Considering the importance of sustainability in all facets of life, this year’s theme of the Management Case Conference will be “Bridging Theory and Practice: Real-World Management Challenges”. The event will be held in hybrid mode. Topics: We invite case study submissions across all functional and interdisciplinary areas of management, highlighting real-world organizational issues and managerial decision-making. Submission Calendar: The organizing committee welcomes submissions of cases, both teaching and non-teaching, from all areas of business and management. The authors can submit an extended abstract (500 words) for MCC 2026. However, authors who are targeting the Best Case Award need to submit a full case. Submission of Extended Abstract: September 30, 2026 Decision on Acceptance of the Abstract: October 10, 2026 Registration of Authors/Delegates: Open Submission of Full Case (If Competing for MCC Awards): October 15, 2026 Submission Guidelines: All cases submitted for oral presentation at MCC must contain original work that has not been previously presented or scheduled for presentation. If accepted for publication, or if under review, it must not appear in print before the case competition. Font: Times New Roman, Size – 12, double-spaced, with a 1-inch (2.5 cm) margin all around. Figures, graphs, tables, references, and appendices should follow APA style. To facilitate the blind review process, all author identities, including acknowledgments, should be removed. The title page containing the names of the authors and affiliations should be submitted separately. The extended abstract should cover the following aspects. Format for Teaching Case: Background Dilemma The Case Data Source Case Questions Teaching Notes Format for Research Case: Purpose Research Question The Case Data Source Methodology Adopted Findings and Contributions Please note that incomplete submissions will not be sent out for the review process. Rules & Guidelines: Eligibility: The competition is open to undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students from recognized colleges, universities, and higher education institutions. Nature of the Case: The presentation should be based on the participant’s Summer Internship Project (SIP) and should present a meaningful managerial/business problem, analysis, findings, and recommendations. Participation: Students may participate individually or in a team of up to 3 members. All team members must be from the same institution. Originality: The submitted work must be original and based on the participant/team’s own SIP experience. Plagiarism, fabrication of information, or misrepresentation of work may lead to disqualification. Confidentiality: Participants must ensure that no confidential or proprietary information of the internship organization is disclosed without appropriate permission. Organization/company names may be anonymized wherever required. Presentation Format: Shortlisted participants/teams will present their case using a PowerPoint presentation (PPT). The presentation should clearly cover the problem/context, objectives, methodology or approach, analysis, key findings, recommendations, and learning/outcomes. description: Overview Organised by: Faculty of Arts & Humanities Mode: Hybrid Date: 26th & 27th February 2027 Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG): SDG 4 Venue: Kalinga University, Kotni, Near Mantralaya, Naya Raipur -…
details_text: Overview Organised by: Faculty of Arts & Humanities Mode: Hybrid Date: 26th & 27th February 2027 Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG): SDG 4 Venue: Kalinga University, Kotni, Near Mantralaya, Naya Raipur - 492101, Chhattisgarh Theme Integration of Indian Knowledge Systems for Sustainable Development and Technological Transformation: Harnessing cultural heritage, social sciences and humanities as foundations for innovation, resilience, and national progress. Concept Note The global landscape is undergoing profound transformations driven by environmental challenges, technological advances, social inequalities, and shifting political dynamics. In this context, the pursuit of a sustainable future requires a multidisciplinary and inclusive approach — one that bridges the spheres of culture, society, and governance. This conference aims to create a vibrant platform for scholars, policymakers, practitioners, and community leaders to engage in critical dialogue about how we can transition toward a more just, resilient, and sustainable world. By examining the intersections of cultural narratives, social systems, and governance models, the event seeks to challenge conventional paradigms and propose innovative solutions to the complex challenges of our time. Culture shapes our values, beliefs, and behaviours; society reflects our collective organisation and resilience; and governance determines how power and resources are distributed. This conference invites contributions that explore emerging trends, indigenous knowledge systems, participatory governance, social justice, and the role of education, media, and the arts in shaping sustainable futures. This Conference Aims To Promote the integration of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) into contemporary education, research, and innovation for holistic and sustainable development. Explore the relevance of traditional Indian knowledge in addressing modern challenges related to sustainability, environmental conservation, and societal well-being. Encourage interdisciplinary research that combines Indian Knowledge Systems with emerging technologies and scientific advancements. Provide a platform for scholars, researchers, academicians, policymakers, and industry experts to exchange ideas, research findings, and best practices on IKS and technological transformation. Identify innovative applications of indigenous knowledge in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, education, energy, environmental management, and entrepreneurship. Foster collaboration among educational institutions, research organisations, industries, and government agencies for the effective implementation of Indian Knowledge Systems in national development. Examine the role of Indian philosophical, ethical, and cultural values in promoting sustainable technologies, responsible innovation, and inclusive growth. Support the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 by encouraging the integration of Indian Knowledge Systems into higher education curricula and research initiatives. Inspire young researchers and students to undertake innovative research that bridges traditional wisdom with modern science and technology. Develop policy recommendations and strategic frameworks for leveraging Indian Knowledge Systems to achieve sustainable development, technological advancement, and the vision of a self-reliant India (Atmanirbhar Bharat). Sub-themes Viksit Bharat @2047 and Humanities Futures: Indian Knowledge Systems as cultural foundations for national vision, identity, and transformation. Governance, Political Thought, and Ethics: Traditions in administration, political science, ethics, and policy innovation. Economic Thought, Rural Humanities, and Geography: Self-reliance, rural transformation, and spatial-cultural development. About the Faculty of Law: The Faculty of Law at Kalinga University, Naya Raipur, is committed to promoting academic excellence and professional development in legal education. With a team of distinguished scholars and experienced faculty members, it provides students with a balanced blend of theoretical knowledge and practical skills required to succeed in the evolving legal profession. Its curriculum is designed to address contemporary legal challenges, enabling students to develop the knowledge and competencies needed to navigate the complexities of today's legal landscape. About the Two-Day Global Conference: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies, reshaping legal systems across the world. From automated decision-making in commercial transactions and predictive policing to AI-generated intellectual property and algorithmic tools in judicial processes, AI continues to redefine governance and legal frameworks. While these technologies promise greater efficiency, innovation, and improved access to justice, they also raise significant concerns relating to accountability, transparency, bias, privacy, liability, and the protection of fundamental human rights. As AI technologies continue to evolve, legal systems across different jurisdictions are adopting diverse regulatory approaches. Questions surrounding the authorship of AI-generated works, criminal liability for autonomous systems, algorithmic discrimination in courts, data protection in healthcare technologies, cross-border cyber risks, and international norms governing autonomous weapons have intensified the need for comparative legal dialogue. The absence of uniform global standards further complicates enforcement, jurisdictional accountability, and regulatory harmonisation. Understanding these multidimensional challenges is essential for developing coherent and future-ready legal frameworks. Comparative legal analysis enables policymakers, researchers, and legal scholars to identify best practices, bridge regulatory gaps, and formulate adaptive legal responses. Commercial law, criminal justice, intellectual property, judicial institutions, healthcare regulation, cyber law, and international legal mechanisms must evolve in a balanced manner that promotes innovation while safeguarding constitutional values and human dignity. details_text: Introducing The Champion's League, DU’s first-ever IPL Auction where strategy meets passion! Step into the role of a club manager, handle a massive budget, and build your dream 11-player squad by bidding live for top Champions League stars. Balance finances, squad composition, and react to real-time News Flashes that impact player ratings. Trade, negotiate, and outwit rivals during transfer windows. It’s a thrilling blend of cricket, finance, and tactics only the smartest manager will claim the Champion's Cup! Rules and Regulations: The event is open to all B-schools and Universities. Each team can have a *minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 members.* Teams can comprise first, second, or third year students, irrespective of their area of specialization. Intercollege teams are encouraged and welcome to come together for collaborative participation. One participant must not be a part of more than one team. All decisions regarding eligibility and final judgment shall rest with the organizing team. Round 1 - Com Quiz (Online) An engaging quiz round will be conducted online via the Unstop app, setting the stage for an intense test of participants’ basic acumen in the world of commerce and the stock market. This round comprises approximately 20 carefully curated questions that challenge each participant’s understanding of key concepts, trends, and strategies in the financial realm. Round 2 -  Champion's League (Offline) Each team will consist of max 4 members, and any change in the lineup requires prior approval from the Organizing Committee. All teams must manage their given budgets carefully overspending will result in disqualification. Every team must complete an 11-player squad covering all positions. “News Flash” twists introduced by organizers may impact player ratings or budgets and cannot be challenged. Final Round -  Final Deal (Offline) Teams Will Deliver an 8–10 Minute Pitch Covering Their Problem, Solution, Target Market, Revenue Model, Financial Projections, and Investment Ask. After the Pitch, a 5-Minute Q&a and Negotiation with The Sharks Will Take Place. Sharks Will Test Ideas, Challenge Valuations, and Push Deal-Making Skills. Teams Must Defend Their Numbers and Decide Wisely Between a Deal, Counter-Offer, or No Deal. General Rules: Teams Must Report on Time for The Auction and Transfer Windows. Late Arrivals May Face Budget Cuts or Reduced Bidding Time as Penalties. The Auctioneer’s Decision Is Final. All Disputes Must Be Raised Immediately. Bidding Must Remain Professional and Fair Throughout the Session. Teams Must Maintain Professionalism, Respect, and Friendly Competition Throughout the Event. During the live auction and transfer windows, the use of external devices (mobiles, laptops, etc.) for real-time market research, financial calculations, or seeking advice from non-participants is strictly prohibited.

details_text: ComStox , hosted by The Commerce Society of SGTB Khalsa College, is a dynamic mock stock competition that attracts participants from colleges and universities nationwide. Through exciting rounds like treasure hunts, auctions, trading simulations, and quizzes, students test their strategic thinking, financial insight, and creativity. Finalists dive into live trading, making real-time decisions to grow their virtual portfolios. ComStox offers a hands-on glimpse into the stock market, allowing students to showcase their analytical skills and competitive spirit. Rules and Regulations: The event is open to all B-schools and Universities. Each team can have a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 members. Teams can comprise first, second, or third year students, irrespective of their area of specialization. Intercollege teams are encouraged and welcome to come together for collaborative participation. One participant must not be a part of more than one team. All decisions regarding eligibility and final judgment shall rest with the organizing team. ROUND 1 - ComQuiz (Online) An engaging quiz round will be conducted online via the Unstop app, setting the stage for an intense test of participants’ basic acumen in the world of commerce and the stock market. This round comprises approximately 20 carefully curated questions that challenge each participant’s understanding of key concepts, trends, and strategies in the financial realm ROUND 2 -  ComStox (Offline) Each team will start with a fixed sum and an equal portfolio of stock.There will be 5-6 rounds in total. Any intentional disruptions initiated by any participating member to disrupt the flow will result in immediate disqualification and/or more stringent actions against the individual. The decision regarding disqualification is final and binding, no further inquiries are entertained on this matter. The organizing team retains the prerogative to alter or amend any of the rules as deemed necessary. The organizers are committed to ensuring fairness and transparency throughout the competition.

title: Barter Mania- " The Ultimate Barter Challenge"
organiser: Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College (ARSD), University of Delhi (DU), New Delhi
description: BARTER MANIA Presented by Commercico, The Commerce Association of Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College Think you know commerce? Time to put it to the test. Commerce isn't just about knowing the numbers. It's about…
details_text: BARTER MANIA Presented by Commercico, The Commerce Association of Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College Think you know commerce? Time to put it to the test. Commerce isn't just about knowing the numbers. It's about understanding markets, spotting opportunities, making decisions under pressure, and knowing when to trade, negotiate or hold your ground. BARTER MANIA is a two-round competition designed to take you from the basics of commerce to the heart of real-world decision-making. From a fast-paced online quiz testing your commerce, finance, general awareness and aptitude to an immersive offline trade and barter challenge , every round will test a different side of your commercial thinking. Because in the real world: Resources are limited. Needs aren't. And the best deal isn't always the obvious one. Think fast. Trade smart. Negotiate better. Are you ready to make the right deal? Stages & Timelines Round 1: The Commerce Sprint- Online Quiz The first round is your entry into the world of BARTER MANIA. A 10-minute online quiz comprising 15 questions will test your basic understanding of: Commerce & business Finance Economics Quantitative aptitude Logical reasoning General awarenes Don't expect an impossible finance exam. The questions are designed to test basic conceptual understanding, awareness and quick thinking. Format: Online Platform: Unstop Questions: 15 Duration: 10 minutes Nature: Eliminatory The highest-performing participants/teams will qualify for the offline round. Round 2: The Trading Floor- Offline Finale This is where commerce leaves the screen. Shortlisted participants will be invited to Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College for a live, on-campus commerce simulation. You will enter a market where resources are scarce, requirements are different and every decision has a price. Teams will be given different resources and financial positions. You'll have to buy, sell, barter, negotiate and strategise to secure the resources you need and maximise your position. The team that understands the market, negotiates the smartest deals and makes the right decisions under pressure will emerge victorious. Mode: Offline Venue: Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College Format: Live Trade & Barter Simulation Final winners: Determined on the basis of performance in the offline round. Who Can Participate? Open to college students Students from all academic backgrounds are welcome Cross-college participation can be allowed Team size: 2-3 A participant can be part of only one team. Rules & Guidelines Round 1 will be conducted online through the Unstop platform. Round 1 will consist of 15 questions to be attempted in 10 minutes . Round 1 will be eliminatory. Shortlisted participants/teams will be informed about the offline round through their registered contact details. The offline round will be conducted at Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, New Delhi . Participants qualifying for Round 2 must be physically present at the venue at the stipulated time. Detailed rules and mechanics of the trade/barter simulation will be communicated before the commencement of Round 2. Any form of malpractice will result in immediate disqualification. The decision of the organising committee shall be final and binding in all matters. The organisers reserve the right to modify the format, timelines or structure of the competition, if required. Further details regarding the offline round will be shared through the official LinkedIn page of the Commerce Association, ARSD College. Participants are requested to follow the page and stay updated. https://www.linkedin.com/company/commercico-the-commerce-association-of-arsdc/

details_text: About the Event Welcome to Chakravyuh: The Escape Challenge, an exciting and interactive puzzle-solving competition where logic, teamwork, creativity, and quick thinking are the keys to victory. Participants will face a series of mysterious clues, coded messages, riddles, and mind-bending challenges. Each solved puzzle will bring them closer to the final escape, but they must stay alert, think strategically, and work together to complete the challenge within the given time limit. Get ready to test your intelligence, challenge your problem-solving skills, and experience an exciting adventure filled with suspense and surprises. Do you have what it takes to solve the mysteries and escape the Chakravyuh? Event Format – The Six Stages of Chakravyuh Chakravyuh: The Escape Challenge is a six-stage, interconnected puzzle-solving experience where every clue matters. Each round is linked to the next, and participants must use the information gathered in previous stages to progress further. Teams will need to think critically, identify hidden patterns, decode messages, and connect seemingly unrelated clues to uncover the final solution. Round 1: The First Clue The journey begins with an introductory puzzle containing hidden hints, symbols, or a QR-based clue. Teams must analyze the information carefully to discover the first key that will lead them into the Chakravyuh. Round 2: Decode the Message Using the clue obtained in Round 1, teams must decipher an encoded message or crack a cipher. The decoded information will reveal an important hint required to proceed to the next stage. Round 3: The Hidden Connection Participants must identify patterns, connect pieces of information, and solve a logic-based challenge. The solution will help them uncover the next clue hidden within the chain of puzzles. Round 4: The Mystery Trail Teams must use the information collected from previous rounds to follow a trail of clues. Careful observation, logical reasoning, and attention to detail will be essential to identify the correct path forward. Round 5: The Final Key All the clues gathered throughout the previous stages will become important. Teams must combine the information, solve a more complex puzzle, and discover the key needed to unlock the final challenge. Round 6: Escape the Chakravyuh The final stage brings the entire journey together. Teams must use the knowledge, codes, and clues collected across all five previous rounds to solve the ultimate puzzle. The team that successfully cracks the final challenge within the given time and meets the event's scoring criteria will emerge victorious. The Challenge Every round is connected, and no clue should be ignored. Speed alone will not guarantee victory; observation, teamwork, logical thinking, and the ability to connect information across all six stages will determine success. Can your team uncover the complete mystery and escape the Chakravyuh? Rules and Guidelines Participants must complete the registration process before the deadline. Participants must follow the team size specified by the organizers. All challenges must be completed within the allotted time. Damaging event materials or props is strictly prohibited. Unauthorized external assistance and sharing of answers between teams are not permitted. Participants must follow the instructions provided by the event coordinators. The use of mobile phones or the internet will not allowed. The winner will be determined according to the announced scoring criteria and challenge completion time. In case of a tie, the organizers may use a tie-breaker round or completion time to determine the result. The organizers' decision regarding the competition and results will be final. Why Participate? Build your robot, compete against another team, and see how well your design holds up under pressure. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering (Fr. details_text: Overview Where Artificial Intelligence Meets Real-World Impact About the Competition The AI Directive is a one-round problem-solving competition for people who believe technology should serve society. Your challenge is to pick a real social or environmental problem, build an AI-powered solution for it, and show how it could create measurable change. We're looking for solutions that are practical, scalable, feasible and responsible. AI should be the core engine of your idea, not an add-on. Choose Your Challenge Area AI for Education and Skill Development AI for Healthcare and Public Health AI for Accessibility and Inclusion AI for Waste Management and Circular Economy AI for Climate Action and Environmental Sustainability AI for Traffic Management and Urban Mobility AI for Rural Development and Entrepreneurship AI for Mental Wellness and Social Well-being AI for Women and Child Safety AI for Financial and Digital Inclusion AI for Disaster Management and Resilience AI for Food Security and Agriculture Have a different idea? You can propose your own social or environmental challenge, as long as it has a clear real-world application and meaningful scope for AI. What Your Submission Must Cover Problem: What is the specific problem? Who is affected, why does it matter, and where do current solutions fall short? AI Solution: What is your idea, what role does AI play, and how is it better than existing approaches? Implementation: How will it work in practice? Cover target users, technology, resources, strategy and likely challenges. Impact: What are the expected benefits and measurable outcomes? How does it scale, and what is its long-term potential? Submission Guidelines Single round, online submission. Register through Unstop. The WhatsApp group link for updates and instructions will be shared there (https://chat.whatsapp.com/IiimeexcRAt4BGMeJ7nSpD). After registering, submit your PowerPoint presentation (PPT) through the designated Google Drive link. The PPT must clearly present the problem, AI solution, implementation strategy and expected impact. Supporting material is welcome: prototype, workflow, UI/UX mock-up or research document. A video pitch is not mandatory. ️ The PPT must be entirely original and must not be AI-generated. While AI must be used meaningfully in your solution, the content, analysis and explanations in your presentation must reflect your team's own ideas and effort. Plagiarism, copied content or submitting another team's work will lead to disqualification. Important Dates Last Date for Registration: 14 October 2026 Last Date for PPT Submission: 15 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST Late submissions may not be considered, so don't leave it to the last minute! Evaluation Criteria Problem Understanding: 20% Effective Use of AI: 25% Innovation and Creativity: 20% Feasibility and Implementation: 20% Social/Environmental Impact and Scalability: 15% Total: 100% Judges will look at how clearly you understand the problem, how meaningfully AI is integrated, how original your approach is, how practical the implementation is, and how much measurable impact it can create. Core Principle Identify a real problem. Build an intelligent solution. Prove it can create real impact. If you could use AI to solve one real-world problem, what would you solve, and how? Register now and show us your answer.

details_text: Overview Have an idea that can solve a real-world problem? It's time to go OFF SCRIPT! OFF SCRIPT 2026 is a pan-India student innovation challenge organised by CSJMU Innovation Foundation to encourage creativity, entrepreneurial thinking, problem-solving, and practical innovation. The event provides students with an opportunity to transform their ideas into practical solutions, develop prototypes, and present their innovations before a jury. Participants can choose between two themes: solving an organiser-provided problem statement or exploring an open innovation challenge based on a problem of their own choice. Whether your idea focuses on technology, agriculture, healthcare, education, sustainability, business, or social impact, OFF SCRIPT welcomes innovative thinking from every domain. Themes of the Challenge Theme 1: Problem Statement (PS) Challenge Participants will work on a problem statement released by the organisers and propose an innovative, feasible, and impactful solution. Problem Statement Release: 15 October 2026 Participants should study the released problem statement and develop a solution addressing the specified challenge. The solution should demonstrate originality, practical feasibility, and potential impact. Theme 2: Open Innovation Challenge Participants can identify a real-world problem of their choice and propose an original solution. There is no restriction to a particular domain. Ideas related to technology, agriculture, healthcare, education, sustainability, environment, business, accessibility, and social innovation are welcome. Participants should clearly explain the problem, their proposed solution, its uniqueness, feasibility, and expected impact. Important: Participants must indicate which theme they are participating in, wherever the registration form provides that option. Event Structure OFF SCRIPT 2026 consists of two rounds. Round 1: Online Idea/PPT Submission Registration Opens: 15 October 2026 Problem Statement Release: 15 October 2026 PPT Submission Deadline: 25 October 2026 Shortlisting Results: 26 October 2026 Participants must register and submit a PowerPoint presentation explaining their proposed solution under their selected theme. The PPT should ideally cover: Problem Statement Proposed Solution Innovation and Unique Selling Proposition (USP) Target Users or Beneficiaries How the Solution Works Feasibility and Implementation Plan Expected Impact or Market Potential Future Scope The jury will evaluate the submissions based on innovation, originality, problem-solution fit, feasibility, and potential impact. Selected teams will be shortlisted for the offline grand finale at CSJMU, Kanpur. The shortlisted teams will be announced on 26 October 2026. PPT Submission Template: To be shared by the organisers. Round 2: Offline Grand Finale Date: 31 October 2026 Venue: Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University (CSJMU), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh Shortlisted teams will present their ideas and prototypes before the jury at the CSJMU campus. Teams are expected to prepare their prototypes or minimum viable products (MVPs) between 26 October and 31 October 2026. Participants should be ready to demonstrate how their solutions work, explain their technical or practical approach, and answer questions from the jury. Tentative Schedule — 31 October 2026 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM: Participant reporting, inauguration, welcome address, and opening activities 12:00 PM onwards: Pitching sessions and prototype presentations By 5:00 PM: Final results announcement and recognition of winners The detailed schedule and reporting instructions will be communicated to shortlisted teams by the organisers. Eligibility and Team Formation Open to students from colleges and universities across India. Each team must consist of 2–4 members. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialisation teams are allowed. Students from different academic backgrounds are encouraged to collaborate. Teams must provide accurate registration details.

details_text: ₹10 Startup is an entrepreneurial competition that challenges participants to design a real, scalable, and sustainable business built around a core product or service priced at just ₹1, ₹5, or ₹10. The objective is not simply to create something inexpensive, but to develop a smart business model that makes affordability compatible with profitability. Teams must demonstrate how their venture can deliver genuine value to customers at an exceptionally low price while generating revenue and achieving long-term growth . Participants are expected to think like entrepreneurs by identifying market needs, understanding consumer behaviour, minimising costs, and developing innovative revenue models that can sustain the business as it scales. The central challenge is to prove that a low-priced offering can become a profitable business through smart execution, repeat purchases, and a well-designed revenue strategy. The Challenge Teams must conceptualise a business whose core product or service is sold at ₹1, ₹5, or ₹10. Their business idea must demonstrate how the chosen price can be maintained while building a financially viable venture. Teams must address four fundamental aspects: Product/Service Identify a real customer need and propose a product or service that customers would be willing to purchase at the specified price. Pricing and Cost Structure Explain how the product or service can be offered at ₹1, ₹5, or ₹10. Consider production costs, delivery expenses, operational costs, and other relevant factors. Revenue Model Demonstrate how the business will generate revenue and become profitable. Possible approaches include repeat purchases, advertising, subscriptions, bundles, commissions, partnerships, or premium add-ons. Scalability and Profitability Explain how the venture can attract customers, increase sales, expand its reach, and maintain profitability as the business grows. The strongest ideas will demonstrate a clear understanding of unit economics, customer demand, and the relationship between affordability and sustainable growth. Submission Guidelines The competition will consist of a single round of online PPT submission . Participants must register for the competition through Unstop. The WhatsApp group link will be provided on Unstop for communication, updates, and further instructions. Teams must submit their PowerPoint presentation (PPT) through the designated Google Drive submission link(which will be provided in the WhatsApp group) before the deadline. The PPT must clearly explain the business concept, target customers, pricing strategy, revenue model, unit economics, and scalability. The presentation must demonstrate how the product or service can be sold at ₹1, ₹5, or ₹10 while supporting a financially sustainable business model. Teams should include realistic cost estimates, revenue assumptions, and an explanation of how the venture can achieve profitability at scale. All submissions must be original and developed by the participating teams. AI-generated PPT content and plagiarism are strictly prohibited. Teams must independently develop their business concepts, financial assumptions, written content, and presentations. Copying existing business plans or submitting another team’s work may result in disqualification. Financial estimates must be reasonable and supported by assumptions wherever possible. No live pitching or video submission will be required. Winners will be determined based on the submitted PPTs. PPT Structure Teams should organise their presentation around the following sections: Slide 1 — Problem and Market Opportunity What problem does the business solve? Who are the target customers? Why would customers buy the offering? Slide 2 — The ₹1/₹5/₹10 Offering Product or service description Key features and value proposition Selected selling price: ₹1, ₹5, or ₹10 Slide 3 — Business and Revenue Model How the business will operate Revenue streams Customer acquisition and retention strategy Slide 4 — Unit Econ

description: Turing Track is an autonomous car racing competition organised by the HAM ARC Club, NIT Warangal, as part of Technozion 2026. Inspired by the F1TENTH and RoboRacer formats, participants will design, build, and program a…
details_text: Turing Track is an autonomous car racing competition organised by the HAM ARC Club, NIT Warangal, as part of Technozion 2026. Inspired by the F1TENTH and RoboRacer formats, participants will design, build, and program a small-scale autonomous car to race on a closed circuit without human intervention. The competition focuses on robotics, perception, planning, control, autonomous systems, and motorsport engineering. Open to race car geeks, robotics enthusiasts, and engineering students of all experience levels :) NOTE: Refer the document attached below for complete race guidlines. Competition Format: Stage 1 - Qualifying Time Trial: Each team gets 3 solo timed attempts. Each attempt consists of one timed lap from a standing start, with a maximum duration of 90 seconds. The fastest completed lap counts, with applicable penalties added to the lap time. Teams receive a 5-minute reset period between attempts for battery swaps, software restarts, and parameter adjustments. The top 25% of teams qualify for the finals. Stage 2 - Head-to-Head Finals: Qualified teams compete through an elimination bracket consisting of quarterfinals, semifinals, and the final. Two cars race simultaneously in each heat. Each heat consists of 3 laps with a maximum duration of 2 minutes. The first car to complete 3 laps without disqualification wins. Unsafe or repeated collisions may result in reseeding or a solo run. Track Details: Track length: 40 m. Track width: 1.5 m. Flat, non-slip surface. 20 cm high boundary walls with deliberate gaps. Includes straights, wide turns, and at least one tight chicane. No tunnels. Includes sensing challenges such as spaced walls and phantom LiDAR returns to test autonomous perception and navigation. Race Rules: Cars must start from a complete stop when the red light changes to green or the starting flag is given. A team member may press the physical start button on the car at the start signal. No other manual input is permitted during the race. A false start results in a 5-second penalty. A second false start during the same attempt results in a DNF. The run ends at the chequered flag or light, with timing conducted by marshals. Cars must count their own laps. Teams may only activate the E-Stop during a timed run. Marshals may reposition an off-track or stuck car, subject to a penalty. Each team will receive an official on-site practice window. Pre-mapping is permitted, but final tuning must be completed during official practice. Vehicle Specifications: Maximum dimensions: 60 × 40 × 30 cm. Maximum weight: 5 kg, including the battery. Power source: LiPo/Li-ion only. No combustion engines. No fixed speed limit, provided the vehicle remains controllable. Permitted sensors: LiDAR, camera, IMU, wheel encoders/odometry. GPS/RTK, V2X, track-side beacons, and other similar technologies require prior approval. Any onboard computer may be used, including Jetson, Raspberry Pi, NUC, or custom boards. All processing must be performed onboard. Cloud/offboard computing and remote-control inputs are prohibited during timed runs. Permitted software approaches include ROS/ROS2, F1TENTH stacks, Pure Pursuit, MPC, Reinforcement Learning, Imitation Learning, or custom autonomous systems. Scoring & Penalties: Qualifying rankings are based on the fastest completed lap out of 3 attempts, after applicable penalties. Teams that do not complete a run are ranked below all finishers based on distance travelled. Touching a wall or obstacle below 5 cm: No penalty. Crossing the boundary line: +5 seconds. Crashing into a wall or obstacle by 5 cm or more: +10 seconds. False start: +5 seconds. Marshal repositioning: +15 seconds. 3 or more incidents in one run: DNF. Unsafe behaviour or rule violation: Disqualification. Safety Requirements: Every vehicle must have a functional physical or wireless E-Stop capable of immediately cutting power to the drive motors. The E-Stop will be checked during technical inspection. Vehicles without a working E-Stop will n

title: Bazaar
description: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market! EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market: Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar…
details_text: All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market! EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market: Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar is where you find out which one you are. Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC) as part of E-Summit, Bazaar is a live stock market trading competition for students. Fictional companies, simulated markets, virtual capital. The pressure is real. What Makes Bazaar Different? Forget static prediction games and paper quizzes. Bazaar runs on a trading platform built specifically for this event, with live prices, breaking news and timed sessions where every decision counts. You don't just trade one market, you trade two. First you play as a retail investor, reading charts and reacting to news. Then you step up to the institutional level, where your own orders move prices, bots trade alongside you, and the market pushes back. News reaches you from many sources: newspapers, analysts, insiders and finfluencers. Not all of them deserve your trust, and knowing which to believe is half the game. The Grand Finale is held at E-Summit, so you compete in the same venue as founders, investors and innovators. Who Should Apply? Bazaar is for anyone who follows the markets, enjoys fast decisions, data or strategy, and wants to experience trading without risking real money. You don't need prior trading experience. Beginners can learn from the rulebook and strategy hints shared before the Finale, and experienced traders will find plenty to exploit. Open to [undergraduate and postgraduate] students across India. Cross-college teams are welcome. Competition Structure Bazaar runs across two rounds. Round 1 is an Online Quiz on Unstop, covering stock market basics, financial instruments, chart and news reading, and risk-based reasoning. Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person at the PEC auditorium on 15 November as part of E-Summit. Finalists trade on Bazaar's live platform across two stages: Stage 1: Retail. Start with virtual capital. Trade across a range of instruments using technical tools. Trading happens in timed sessions that get tougher as new instruments and news unlock. Stage 2: Institutional. Start with renewed virtual capital. Now your trades move prices, and bots compete with you for liquidity. Every trade carries a transaction fee, so overtrading will cost you. Teams are ranked on trading performance. General scoring guidelines and a rulebook will be shared with registered teams before the Finale. Prizes & Rewards: 1st Place –  E-Summit Networking Pass | Certificate of Excellence 2nd Place – E-Summit Networking Pass | Certificate of Excellence 3rd Place – Certificate of Excellence All Grand Finale Teams – Certificate of Achievement All Participants – Certificate of Participation Team Details: Team Size: 2 to 4 members Cross-college and cross-city teams: Fully allowed and encouraged Solo registrations: Not accepted One person registers as Team Leader and adds the remaining members on Unstop Round 1: know the market. Round 2: trade it. Beat the Market. Join the WhatsApp Group: https://shorturl.at/YdsqN

details_text: About The Event: A high-stakes cybersecurity tournament that tests participants across three competitive stages, transitioning from general domain knowledge to practical code-breaking and strategic decision-making. Organized to evaluate digital security awareness, analytical problem-solving, and composure under pressure, teams battle through quiz rounds, real-world cipher/phishing challenges, and an interactive grid showdown. Round-wise Details: Round 1: Cyber Scan (Cybersecurity Quiz): Format: Screening Quiz (~20 Questions). Mechanism: Teams answer a range of cybersecurity questions spanning foundational awareness, threat terminology, security protocols, and domain principles. Selection: The Top 20 teams advance to Round 2. Round 2: Threat Trace (Practical Decryption & Phishing Audit): Format: Time-limited pen-and-paper practical sprint. Section A (Decrypt): Teams solve 5 progressive decoding challenges involving Caesar ciphers, Morse code, binary, substitution, emoji ciphers, or QR/image clues—where answers may unlock subsequent clues. Section B (Phishing): Teams audit 5 realistic digital communications (emails, SMS, Discord messages, login pages) to identify red flags and classify them as PHISHING or LEGIT. Selection: The Top 5–7 teams advance to the Grand Finale. Round 3: Cyber Grid (Strategic Buzzer Grid Battle): Format: Interactive category grid & buzzer round. Mechanism: The remaining finalist teams compete across 6 cybersecurity categories containing questions with varying point values selected via a wheel-spinning mechanism. Gameplay: Teams press the designated buzzer to earn answering rights. A correct answer yields the full question value, while an incorrect response or pass incurs negative points. The team with the highest cumulative score wins the championship. Rules And Guidelines: Eligibility & Team Structure: Open to all registered participants. Participation is strictly team-based, and members must remain consistent throughout all rounds. Device & AI Restrictions: Use of electronic devices, laptops, smartphones, search engines, chatbots, or AI tools is strictly prohibited unless explicitly authorized for a specific round. Pen and paper will be used for written/decryption challenges. Buzzer & Grid Mechanics: The first team to buzz gets the initial opportunity to answer. If passed or answered incorrectly, the opportunity moves to the next fastest team. Negative marking applies for incorrect answers or passed opportunities after buzzing. Fair Play & Security Integrity: Sharing answers or collaborating with opposing teams is forbidden. Any attempt to hack, probe, or tamper with competition infrastructure, scoring systems, or event platforms will result in immediate disqualification. Final Authority: In the event of ties or disputes, the decision of the organizing committee is final and binding. details_text: Round Wise Details Round 1: Design Under Pressure Duration: 75–90 Minutes Mechanism: Participants receive an SDG-focused design brief and develop a comprehensive digital campaign concept (visual language, typography, color scheme, imagery hierarchy, and messaging). Round 2: From Screen to Real World Duration: 45–60 Minutes Mechanism: Teams translate their Round 1 campaign identity into a physical fashion merchandise mockup or product line (e.g., streetwear, accessories, apparel branding). The physical application must maintain visual continuity with the digital campaign. The Commercial Twist: Organizers introduce a surprise commercial/manufacturing constraint that teams must resolve while preserving the core SDG message and aesthetic appeal. Final Presentation & Defense Deliverables: Teams submit and present: Original Design: Initial campaign layout. Adapted Design: Final digital iteration after live shifts. Merchandise Application: Physical/fashion product mockup. Pitch (60–90 Seconds): Brief presentation explaining design decisions, brief adaptations, product rationale, and SDG connection. Rules and Guidelines Participation & Structure: Open to individual entries or teams of 2–3 members . Total event duration is approximately 2.5–3 hours. Bringing your own Laptop is Mandatory for all the teams Brief & Identity Consistency: Participants must strictly adhere to the assigned SDG topic and brief requirements. During Round 1 live shifts, teams must adapt existing assets rather than restarting. In Round 2, the fashion product must derive directly from the Round 1 visual identity. Practical Design Execution: Physical/fashion merchandise mockups must consider real-world factors such as printability, composition, scale, and desirability. Submission: All 3 connected design outcomes (Original, Adapted, Merchandise) and the 60–90 second pitch defense are mandatory for evaluation. Judging Criteria: Concept clarity & strength of the SDG social message Speed & impact of visual communication Adaptability under live brief changes Design fundamentals (typography, composition, color theory, hierarchy) Seamless transition into fashion/physical merchandise Pitch presentation and design justification Final Authority: The decision of the judges and organizing committee is final and non-contestable.

details_text: About The Event: IoTopia: Hardware Expo is an IoT and hardware exhibition where student innovators showcase functional hardware projects addressing critical real-world challenges through IoT, embedded systems, smart automation, and sustainable technologies. The expo is aligned with the following United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being: Smart healthcare systems, health monitoring, and safety devices. SDG 7: Affordable And Clean Energy: Energy-efficient automation, smart grids, and renewable energy integration. SDG 11: Sustainable Cities And Communities: Smart urban infrastructure, environmental monitoring, and sustainable automation. Round-wise Details: Online Screening Round: Format: Online PPT Submission. Mechanism: Registered teams submit a detailed slide deck outlining their project concept, problem statement, hardware architecture, circuit/block diagrams, and SDG alignment for initial screening and shortlisting. Offline Round — Hardware Expo & Live Demo: Format: Physical prototype exhibition & live presentation. Mechanism: Shortlisted teams set up their hardware project booth at the venue, display a project poster (A1/A2 size), and perform live working demonstrations before a panel of judges, followed by a Q&A session. Rules And Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to all currently enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students. Cross-college teams are permitted, but each participant can belong to only one team. A valid college ID card is mandatory. Team Size: 1 to 4 members per team. Hardware & Prototype Requirements: Projects must be physically built and working utilizing microcontrollers/microprocessors (Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, STM32, etc.), sensors, actuators, and active connectivity modules. Simulation-only or software-only projects are strictly prohibited. Projects must be original. Buying off-the-shelf, fully ready-made products will lead to instant disqualification. Pre-built kits are permitted only if substantial original engineering and custom logic are demonstrated. Live demonstrations are required; pre-recorded videos serve purely as a secondary backup. Booth & Equipment Requirements: Teams must bring their own components, laptops, extension boards, cables, and power banks. Basic power outlets and Wi-Fi will be provided. Each team must present a poster (A1/A2 size) detailing the project title, problem, solution, SDG mapping, and circuit/system block diagram. Safety & Restrictions: Open flames, hazardous chemicals, dangerous materials, or high-voltage setups (above 230V) are strictly prohibited. Plagiarism of code, circuit designs, or ideas without proper credit is forbidden. Judging Criteria: Innovation and Originality Technical Complexity & Working Prototype Execution SDG Alignment & Social Impact Practicality, Scalability & Cost-Effectiveness Presentation, Poster Quality & Q&A Response Overall System Design, Finish & Safety Tie-breaker: Higher score in Technical Complexity, followed by Q&A performance. title: Bio-Economy Hackathon 2026 (Kolkata)
description: Bio Economy Hackathon One campus, one day, six bio-economy tracks - student teams build implementable solutions for India's growing bioeconomy, hosted on forested ground at ZSI Kolkata Date: 2 November 2026, Monday ·…
details_text: Bio Economy Hackathon One campus, one day, six bio-economy tracks - student teams build implementable solutions for India's growing bioeconomy, hosted on forested ground at ZSI Kolkata Date: 2 November 2026, Monday · 08:00–18:30 Venue: Zoological Survey of India, Kolkata Format: One-day, in person. Registration & kits from 8 AM Teams: 1-4 members. Solo sign-ups welcome About the Series: Part of a national IEDC hackathon series taken to four regions of India, this South-region edition brings student innovators, early-stage entrepreneurs, and faculty mentors together to prototype solutions across agri-biotech, bioenergy, biopharma, blue economy, forest economy, and biomaterials sectors - sectors the Government of India is actively growing as a share of GDP. About the Venue: The Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) is India's main government body for studying and documenting the country's animal life. It was founded on 1 July 1916, is headquartered in Kolkata at the Indian Museum complex, and operates under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Its work centers on surveying and identifying animal species across India's varied habitats, discovering and describing new ones, and maintaining the National Zoological Collections, a large reference repository of preserved specimens. It also publishes research (such as the Fauna of India series), supports conservation with data on species distribution and endangered animals, helps agencies like customs and wildlife enforcement identify species, and offers training and public outreach. The Kolkata headquarters coordinates regional centres across the country, each focusing on local fauna. Overall, ZSI is central to knowing what animal species India has, where they live, and how they are doing. Six Bio-Economy Tracks: Agri-biotech & precision farming: Crop-yield prediction, biofertilisers & biopesticides, soil-health diagnostics. Bioenergy & waste-to-wealth: Agri-residue valorisation, biogas/biofuel systems, organic waste management. Biopharma & healthcare biotech: Low-cost diagnostics, herbal & nutraceutical formulations, biosensors. Blue economy: Seaweed cultivation, fisheries by-product use, aquaculture technology. Forest-based bioeconomy: NTFP value addition, medicinal-plant supply chains, eco-tourism tech. Bioplastics & biomaterials: Biodegradable packaging, natural-fibre composites, sustainable materials. Regional Priority Track - Weighted toward forest-based bioeconomy: All six tracks are open to every team; Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) Kolkata edition additionally curates 2–3 priority problem statements around forest economy and NTFP value chains, drawing on the host institute's own domain. Event-Day Schedule: 08:00 – 09:00: Registration and kit distribution 09:00 – 09:45: Inaugural session: welcome address, chief guest 09:45 – 10:30: Keynote: "Bio Economy Opportunities and National Priorities" 10:30 – 11:00: Rules briefing, team check-in, problem-statement lock-in 11:00 – 13:00: Hacking session 1: ideation and prototype / solution building 13:00 – 14:00: Lunch break 14:00 – 16:00: Hacking session 2: with rotating mentor check-ins per team 16:00 – 16:30: Submission deadline, pitch deck / prototype finalisation 16:30 – 17:30: Final pitches & demos: 5-minute pitch, 3-minute Q&A per team 17:30 – 17:50: Judges' deliberation 17:50 – 18:30: Valedictory session: feedback, prizes and certificates Judging Criteria - 100 Points: Bio-economy relevance & impact: 25% Innovation & originality: 20% Technical / scientific feasibility: 20% Scalability & commercial viability: 20% Presentation & clarity: 15% Who Can Join: Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students, any discipline; mixed-discipline teams encouraged. Team size: 3-4 members. Individual registration is fine - teams are formed at orientation. Panel: 2 academics, 1 industry judge, 1 government / state startup-mission representative. Prizes: First Place: ₹15,000 Second Place: ₹10,000 Third Place: ₹5,000

title: Roverra — Build Your Own Planetary Rover
organiser: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Delhi
description: Roverra: ROVERRA is a hands-on robotics competition based on the theme of Moon/Mars exploration. Participants will work in teams to assemble a basic robotic rover using components and kits available with the club and…
details_text: Roverra: ROVERRA is a hands-on robotics competition based on the theme of Moon/Mars exploration. Participants will work in teams to assemble a basic robotic rover using components and kits available with the club and then operate their rover on a specially designed planetary terrain course. The workshop will simulate a simplified Moon/Mars surface and will contain different difficulty levels, such as slopes, uneven terrain, rocky sections, narrow passages, turns, checkpoints and crater-like obstacles. Teams will be given a limited time to assemble and test their rover. The objective is to successfully navigate the complete workshop in the minimum possible time while avoiding obstacles and penalties. The event will encourage participants to learn practical robotics, mechanical assembly, electronics, motor control, teamwork and problem-solving. Event Format: Expected participation: 150+ participants. Duration: 3.5 hours. Team size: Maximum 4 participants. Teams assemble a basic rover kit using available club components. Teams test their rover before the final timed challenge. Final ranking will be based on successful workshop completion, time and applicable penalties. Winners will be awarded with goodies.

details_text: Robo Soccer: Robo Soccer is a competitive robotics event where participants control pre-built robots to play football in specially designed miniature soccer fields. The event is intended as a Next day activity after the rover-based event. The major advantage is that the club already has the robots, so participants do not need to build a robot from scratch. Instead, they will focus on robot control, coordination, strategy, navigation and competitive gameplay. The venue will contain 3 separate Robo Soccer fields so that multiple matches can take place simultaneously. This parallel-field setup will allow the event to accommodate 100+ participants within the planned 3-hour duration. Teams will participate in short football matches. Depending on the final number of participants and available robots, the competition can be organized into qualification/group matches followed by knockout rounds. Event Format: Expected participation: 100+ participants. Duration: 3 hours. 3 parallel miniature soccer fields. Existing club robots will be used. Short matches to allow a large number of teams to participate. Match rules will define field boundaries, match duration, scoring, robot limits and penalties. Goodies will be given.
