details_text: HACK INTO PCELL v2.0 (Build. Break. Solve.) is a multi-stage technical challenge combining campus exploration, digital puzzles, system investigation, and problem-solving. Teams start with an ESP32-based treasure hunt, discovering checkpoints and cracking clues to progress. The top teams advance to SYSTEM//BREAK, an offline terminal-based challenge where participants investigate a simulated environment, analyze issues, and solve technical challenges via the command line. Eligibility & Team Guidelines: Team Size: Exactly 3 members per team. Participation: Open to both Intra-College and Inter-College students. Inter-College Teams: Allowed. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (subject to the institutional cap of maximum 2 teams per class). Class Limit: A maximum of 2 teams are permitted from each class. First Year (FE) Category: Evaluated separately through Level 1; does not proceed to Level 2. A dedicated FE Winner is selected directly from Level 1 performance. External Participants: 2 external team slots are reserved for Level 2. An orientation video covering the college layout will be shared one week prior. Registration Fee: ₹200 per team. Competition Format & Rounds: Level 1: ESP32 Treasure Hunt Date: 29th October 2026 Venue: Room 305 & designated areas (3rd floor and below) Duration: 1 hour Number of Checkpoints / Problem Statements: Up to 15 physical ESP32 Wi-Fi checkpoints; 15 flag submissions required. Description: Teams locate physical ESP32 Wi-Fi checkpoints across campus, solve the associated puzzles/challenges, and submit flags on the event portal. Allowed Resources: Smartphones with Wi-Fi capability/Wi-Fi analyser apps, search engines, AI tools, and the internet are allowed. Advancement: The top 10 regular teams qualify for Level 2. Level 2: SYSTEM//BREAK Date: 30th October 2026 Venue: Room 312 Environment: Controlled, offline terminal-based environment with no internet access. Focus Areas: Basic Linux commands, system analysis, file hierarchies, logs, processes, network information, permissions, and logical dependencies. Allowed Resources: A generic SYSTEM//BREAK reference manual will be provided beforehand. Strictly NO internet, NO AI tools, NO search engines, and NO external assistance. Evaluation & Scoring Policy: Level 1: Ranked primarily by the number of successful flag submissions. Recorded flag completion/submission time serves as the tiebreaker. Level 2: Ranked by the number of challenges successfully resolved within the offline terminal environment. Time taken serves as the tiebreaker to determine 1st and 2nd place. Rules & Disqualification Criteria: Team Collaboration: Collaboration is strictly limited to registered members of your own team during active rounds. Fair Play: Any cheating, sabotage, network tampering, unauthorized system access, or sharing information across teams results in immediate disqualification. Disqualification Triggers: Cheating or unauthorized external assistance. Unauthorized system, network, or restricted physical area access. Tampering with event infrastructure, checkpoints, or equipment. Manipulating submission timestamps or exploiting unintended platform bugs. Unsportsmanlike, disruptive, or unsafe behaviour. Unauthorized team-member substitutions. Authority: Decisions made by Project Cell organizers and officials are final and binding in all matters.

title: Agnirakshak - Autonomous Fire Fighting Bot Challenge.
organiser: Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering (FRCRCE), Bandra
description: AGNIRAKSHAK is an autonomous firefighting robotics competition that challenges participants to design and build a robot capable of independently navigating a specially designed obstacle arena, detecting and…
details_text: AGNIRAKSHAK is an autonomous firefighting robotics competition that challenges participants to design and build a robot capable of independently navigating a specially designed obstacle arena, detecting and extinguishing four candle-based fire sources, and reaching the designated finish zone in the shortest possible time. The competition tests participants on robotics, autonomous navigation, sensing, control systems, and problem-solving. The robot must operate completely autonomously once the run begins, without any manual control or physical assistance from the team. Eligibility & Team Formation The competition is open to students with an interest in robotics, automation, and engineering. Teams must consist of 2-3 members Each team must register with a unique team name and designated team members. Participants must carry a valid college/institution ID for verification. Competition Format The competition will be conducted in two rounds: Round 1 – Qualifying Round 16 teams will compete. Each team gets one run. The robot must navigate the arena, locate and extinguish the fire sources, and reach the finish zone. The top 8 teams will qualify for the final round based on the competition ranking criteria. Round 2 – Final Round The top 8 teams will compete. Each finalist gets up to two valid runs. A team's better run will be considered for the final ranking. Teams will be ranked primarily on the number of candles extinguished, followed by total time and number of penalties. Objective The robot must: Navigate the arena autonomously. Detect and locate the designated candle-based fire sources. Extinguish up to four candles. Successfully reach the finish zone. Complete the challenge within the prescribed time limit Scoring & Penalties Ranking priority will be: Number of candles extinguished – Higher is better. Total time taken – Lower is better. Number of penalties – Lower is better.

title: OHM MY GOD! IEEExWIE_CRCE

details_text: Think you can decode a circuit, make the right engineering decisions, and bring it to life? OHM MY GOD! , organized by IEEExWIE CRCE under CRESCENDO 2026 , is a team-based technical electronics challenge designed to test participants’ circuit understanding, datasheet interpretation, component selection, problem-solving, and hands-on circuit-building skills. The competition consists of three consecutive phases: DECODE – Analyze and complete an incomplete circuit using the provided datasheets. DECIDE – Select suitable components for a given application within a virtual budget. BUILD – Use the selected components to build, test, and demonstrate a working circuit. Guidelines Inter-College Teams: All 3 participants must belong to the same academic year . Each team must have exactly 3 participants . Registration fee is ₹150 per team . The competition is scored out of 100 marks across all three phases. All required components, datasheets, and basic testing resources will be provided by the organizers. Rules All participants must follow the official queue/order assigned by the organizers. Work beyond the applicable maximum cap shall not be permitted. The exact completion time for every phase shall be officially recorded. Teams shall attempt all tasks independently. Mobile phones, internet access, AI tools, and unauthorized reference material are prohibited during active competition. Only datasheets/reference material officially provided by the organizers may be used. Participants shall not communicate answers, circuit connections, or solutions to other teams. Personal electronic components and pre-built circuits/modules are prohibited. Only components and equipment authorized by the organizers may be used. Judges shall not provide technical assistance, hints, or component-selection confirmation. Phase 2 component selection shall be entirely the responsibility of the participating team. Selected components shall be carried forward to Phase 3. Once a team requests an official circuit check in Phase 1 or Phase 3, it will be counted as an attempt. The number of checking attempts shall be determined by the announced participation condition. Participants must follow laboratory and electrical safety instructions. Judges' decisions regarding circuit correctness and output shall be final. The judges’ decision regarding scoring, circuit output, and results will be final.

title: Fr.CRCE Shark Tank 2026

description: Fr.CRCE Shark Tank is a student entrepreneurship competition that gives aspiring founders a platform to present their business ideas and experience what it takes to face real-world investor questions. Participants will…
details_text: Fr.CRCE Shark Tank is a student entrepreneurship competition that gives aspiring founders a platform to present their business ideas and experience what it takes to face real-world investor questions. Participants will take their ideas beyond just a concept and present their problem statement, solution, target market, business model, competition, revenue potential, scalability, and financial projections. The competition is designed to test not only the idea, but also how well a team understands the business behind it. The competition begins with a screening round based on the pitch decks submitted by participating teams. The shortlisted teams move forward to the National-Level Grand Finale , where they will face the Sharks in one integrated round combining pitching, valuation, investment, Q&A, and negotiation. The Final Round features a mock investment simulation, putting teams in the shoes of real founders. Teams will set their startup valuation, decide how much investment they need, and determine the equity they are willing to offer before defending their numbers and negotiating with the Sharks. Sharks may accept the proposal, make a counter-offer, reject it, or restructure the deal. The competition is an opportunity to put your business knowledge, communication, financial thinking, decision-making, and negotiation skills to the test with a total prize pool of ₹60,000 waiting for the teams that stand out. Have an idea? Bring it to the table. The Sharks are waiting . Guidelines : Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate college students Team Size: Minimum 2, Maximum 4 members Venue: Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering, Bandstand, Bandra (W), Mumbai Dates and Duration: 30th October (Final Round) | 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM Registration Fee: ₹149 per team Registration Deadline: 18th October Note: Not for Fr.CRCE Students Rules: Teams must report at the start of the event Maximum 4 members per team Valid ID Cards and confirmation receipts mandatory Plagiarism of ideas leads to disqualification Misbehavior results in disqualification Sharks’ decisions are final and binding Real investments/mentorships are separate from the simulated equity game Dress Code: Strictly formal or product-themed attire Presentation must be technically compatible with event equipment Product prototypes are recommended Judging Criteria: Business Model Scalability Pitch Negotiation Skills Creativity Originality Sales Projection

organiser: Fr. Conceicao Rodrigues College of Engineering (FRCRCE), Bandra
description: Formula Unicorn goes beyond a conventional business competition. Teams are placed in a simulated entrepreneurial environment where every decision matters, from the companies you acquire and the price you pay to the…
details_text: Formula Unicorn goes beyond a conventional business competition. Teams are placed in a simulated entrepreneurial environment where every decision matters, from the companies you acquire and the price you pay to the business you build. Starting with ₹100 Crores in virtual money, teams compete in a strategic auction, identify synergies between their acquisitions, and turn them into a meaningful, innovative and viable business concept . The final challenge is to turn that idea into a prototype and pitch it before the judges, as well as the competing teams. The Challenge: Bid → Acquire → Integrate → Build → Pitch Eligibility & Team Structure Team size: 2-3 participants Open to inter-college participation Maximum 30 teams: 20 internal (expandable if needed) and 10 external Only one team per class can participate. If the 30-team limit is not reached, additional internal teams may be allowed to join External teams must clear a shortlisting round (Round 0) before the final event Round 0 : Shortlisting (External Teams Only) Shortlisting is based on the resumes of team members Shortlisted teams are selected for Round 1 Round 1: Auction (29th October) Budget: ₹100 Crores per team; acquire a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 companies Format: 5 min company auction with a 30 sec cooling period Only the team leader can raise the bidding placard Teams acquiring fewer than 2 companies are eliminated Special Auction Rule: If only one team remains interested in a company, the auctioneer raises the price once more. If the team accepts, it buys at that price; if it declines, it still wins the company at the earlier lower price Twists along the way: Market Shock, Mystery Company, Insider Information, Trade Window, Hidden Synergy and Curveball Constraint Round 2: Product Integration & Pitch (30th October) Create a product, service, business or merger using your acquisitions The presentation must follow the template provided by E-Cell CRCE Each qualified team presents its final business idea to the judges Format: 8 min presentation + 2-3 min investor Q&A Other participants can raise questions to the presenting team. If the presenting team fails to reply satisfactorily, it will lose points and the team that asked the question will gain additional points Teams must carry their own laptops and a presentation backup. Figma or other digital mock-ups can be used, while actual prototypes are encouraged Evaluation Criteria (in no particular order) : Problem being addressed Target market Existing competitors in the space Proposed solution Business model Prototype & mock-up (even a Figma presentation works) Estimated revenue targets Future expansion scope Presentation skills Venue & Schedule 29th October, Round 1: Seminar Hall 108, 10 AM onwards 30th October, Round 2: Classroom 608, 10 AM onwards Registration Fee ₹250 per team Before the Auction The company list and base prices (up to 40 companies) will be released at 8 PM, one evening before the event A rules video will be shared in the official WhatsApp group at 8 PM, one day before Team numbers and seating are decided by the council A 3-company mock auction will be held before the actual auction Recognition 1st Place 2nd Place FE Winner (within CRCE) Plus certificates, goodies and snacks Disputes Under any disputes, E-Cell CRCE remains the de facto body for resolving disputes. details_text: AeroCraft is an aerospace design and innovation challenge that puts your engineering thinking to the test. Participants will be given an aerospace-oriented problem statement and challenged to develop a virtual CanSat solution using digital design and modelling tools. Teams must develop their solution within the specified time limit. Participants may use suitable CAD/3D modelling software. Laptop setups will also be available at the venue. FOR CRCE  Teams participation limit per class : 2 Teams Rules: All submitted work must be original and created by the participating team. Teams must strictly follow the requirements and constraints given in the problem statement. Teams must submit their work within the specified time limit . Only registered team members are permitted to participate in the competition. Any form of misconduct, misrepresentation, or violation of the competition rules may result in disqualification.

title: Founder's Trail
description: Founder’s Trail is an entrepreneurship challenge by E-Cell, IIT Patna , where participants take a startup idea from identifying a real world problem to developing, validating, and taking it to the market. The challenge…
details_text: Founder’s Trail is an entrepreneurship challenge by E-Cell, IIT Patna , where participants take a startup idea from identifying a real world problem to developing, validating, and taking it to the market. The challenge is divided into 3 rounds : Discover, Design , and Deliver with each round building on the previous one. Team Size: Participation requires teams of 1-3 people . Round 1: Discover Start with a real problem and develop a startup idea around it. Your task is to show that the problem actually exists, understand your target customers, and support your idea with proper market research. Deliverables: Problem Statement - What problem are you solving and for whom? Startup Idea - Your proposed solution and how it solves the problem. Startup Domain - Identify the industry/domain in which your startup operates . Target Customers - Define your primary customer segment and their key needs or pain points. Market Research - Primary/secondary research, customer insights and relevant data. Competitor Analysis - Existing competitors, alternatives and your differentiation. Startup Identity - Startup name, logo and a basic brand identity representing your idea. Idea Submission - A concise document/presentation combining the above. Round 2: Design Now turn your idea into a practical and viable venture and plan how you will take it to your first customers. Participants will define the solution, business model, pricing and a clear GTM (Go-To-Market) strategy. Deliverables: Solution Design - Product/service concept, prototype or working model. Customer Journey - How the customer discovers, uses and receives value from your solution. Business Model - Pricing, basic costs and how the venture will generate revenue. GTM Strategy - Target customers, acquisition channels and conversion strategy. Submission - Present the complete venture and its execution plan with the above requirements. Round 3: Deliver The final stage challenges teams to take their venture beyond planning and test it in the real world. Teams will execute their marketing strategy, reach potential customers, and collect real world feedback to evaluate and improve their venture Marketing & Execution Guidelines: Content & Social Media Creation: Create and publish promotional Reels and short-form content on your project's dedicated Instagram account. Ensure you use the official event hashtag and tag @ecell_iitpatna in all posts. Customer Acquisition: Reach customers beyond social media using other outreach methods, campus groups and product demos. Tracking & Metrics: Measure success by monitoring views, engagement, inquiries, qualified leads. Iteration & Improvement: How you will use performance data and customer feedback to refine your messaging and continuously improve your venture. How Selection Works Every round is an elimination round , and only the top performing teams advance to the next round. A judging panel evaluates each submission based on the criteria specified for that round. Round wise deliverables, submission guidelines, and judging criteria will be provided at the beginning of each round. Teams must prepare their pitch decks according to the specified deliverables and slide limits for that round. Ties will be broken based on the higher score in the first criterion listed in the respective round's evaluation table. Note : For every round, teams must submit a pitch deck within the slide limit specified for that round and follow all deliverables mentioned in the respective round guidelines.For queries , you can contact any of the organisers.

details_text: Eligibility: The competition is open to college/university students only . Students from any college, university, branch, or specialization are eligible. This is an individual competition . Team participation is not allowed. Participants may choose any form of performance, provided that it is related to technology . Format: Each participant will be given 1 minute and 30 seconds to perform their act on stage. Participants are free to choose the format of their performance, as long as it has a clear connection to technology. Possible performance formats include: Tech poetry Tech comedy or stand-up Tech roast Roasting your own startup/project Technology-related storytelling Tech parody Any other creative technology-related act Before their performance, the participant will provide their self-rating to the organising team. After the performance, the participant may interact with the host/judges. Judging: Performance: The participant performs their chosen technology-related act within the allotted 1 minute and 30 seconds . Self-Rating: Before their performance, the participant gives themselves a score from 1 to 10 . Judges' Scoring: Each judge independently gives the participant a score from 1 to 10 , based on the quality, creativity, execution, and overall impact of the performance. Judges' Average: The scores given by all judges are averaged to calculate the final judges' score. The Verdict: If the participant's self-rating exactly matches the judges' average score , the participant wins the designated reward for that round. Rules: Participation is strictly individual . No team performances are allowed. The performance must have a clear technology-related theme or connection . Participants are free to choose the format and style of their act. Participants must provide their self-rating from 1 to 10 before their performance. The judges' scores will be averaged to determine the final score. A participant wins the round's designated reward only if their self-rating exactly matches the judges' average score . Participants must not attempt to influence or communicate with the judges regarding their scores. Performances must remain appropriate for a college event. Offensive, discriminatory, or excessively inappropriate content may result in disqualification. The judges' decision regarding the performance score will be final and binding . The organizers reserve the right to intervene or disqualify a participant if their performance violates the event rules or disrupts the event. Winner & Rewards: A participant who achieves an exact match between their self-rating and the judges' average score will be eligible for the designated reward for that round. Multiple participants may win rewards if multiple participants achieve an exact match.

title: Worst UI

description: Eligibility: The competition is open to college/university students only . Students from any college, university, branch, or specialization are eligible. This is an individual competition ; participants must compete…
details_text: Eligibility: The competition is open to college/university students only . Students from any college, university, branch, or specialization are eligible. This is an individual competition ; participants must compete independently. Inter-specialization participation is allowed , as there are no restrictions based on academic branch or specialization. Format: The competition will consist of 3–4 rounds . Each round will be independent, and participants can choose to participate in any round they feel is feasible for them. In each round, participants will be given a specific UI/interface or component to design. Participants will be given a fixed time limit for each round to design their interface. The problem statement and time limit for each round will be announced at the beginning of the respective round. At the end of each round, participants will submit/present their designs for evaluation. A winner will be selected for each round. Rules: Participants must compete individually . No teams or collaboration between participants are allowed. The objective is to intentionally create the worst possible/most irritating user interface for the given problem statement while keeping it functional. Designs should be confusing, inconvenient, unintuitive, unnecessarily complex, or creatively frustrating. Participants must work on the problem statement assigned for the respective round. All designs must be created and submitted within the allotted time. Designs must be original and created by the participant during the competition. Plagiarism, copying another participant's work, or collaborating with another participant will result in disqualification. Judging will be based on worst usability, creativity, unnecessary complexity, confusing user experience, and entertainment value . Judging Criteria: Each submission will be evaluated on: Worst Usability – How difficult and frustrating the interface is to use. Creativity – How creatively the participant makes the interface bad. Unnecessary Complexity – The extent of needless complexity introduced. Confusing UX – How unintuitive and confusing the interface is. Entertainment Value – How humorous and entertaining the design is. Winner & Rewards: A winner will be selected for each round. Winners will receive rewards/prizes as decided by the organizing team.

Powered by Unstop | Organized by E-Cell, Great Lakes Institute of Management About the Competition What if you could take apart the business model of a billion-dollar company, identify what makes it successful, find where it can break, and then rebuild it for the future? Business Model Teardown Challenge is an entrepreneurship and strategy competition designed to test how well you understand the businesses shaping today's economy. From Zomato and Blinkit to CRED, Nykaa, boAt and Meesho , participants will go beyond simply studying successful companies. You will tear down their business models, identify opportunities and vulnerabilities, and create a better way forward. This is not just a case competition. It is a test of how you think like an entrepreneur. The Challenge Every successful company has a business model. But every business model has a weakness. Your mission is to: DECODE → TEAR DOWN → IDENTIFY → REBUILD → DEFEND Understand how the business works. Find the crack in the model. Identify an opportunity. Build a better business model. Defend your idea against the jury. Who Can Participate? Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students . Students from any academic discipline or specialization can participate. Participants can register individually or as a team. No prior entrepreneurship experience is required. Team Size 1–3 members per team Competition Structure The competition consists of 3 rounds , and every round is an elimination round. Only the teams that clear one round will move to the next. Round 1 — the Entrepreneurial Iq Online Quiz | Elimination Round Think fast. Think commercially. The first round will test your understanding of entrepreneurship, business models, startups, strategy, marketing, finance and the business ecosystem. Topics may include: Entrepreneurship & startups Business models Revenue models Unit economics Marketing & GTM Startup funding Business strategy Famous startups & companies Innovation Current business trends Format: Online Quiz Mode: Online Questions: 25 MCQ-based Questions Time: 10 Minutes Nature: Elimination Only the top-performing participants/teams will qualify for Round 2. Round 2 — Tear It Down Business Model Analysis & Submission | Elimination Round This is where the real teardown begins. Shortlisted teams will be provided with a company/business model to analyse. Your task is to go beyond describing the company. You need to understand why the business works, where it struggles and how you would rebuild it. Your analysis should cover: 1. Understand the Business Who is the customer? What problem does the company solve? What is its value proposition? How does it acquire customers? How does it make money? 2. Break Down the Economics Revenue streams Cost structure Customer acquisition Unit economics Profitability Scalability 3. Identify the Crack Find one major weakness, risk or untapped opportunity in the existing business model. Ask yourself: "Where can this business model become vulnerable?" 4. Rebuild the Model Now think like the founder. Propose a redesigned business model that can improve the company's: Revenue Profitability Customer acquisition Retention Scalability Competitive advantage 5. Defend Your Idea Your solution should not only be innovative. It should be realistic, commercially viable and scalable. Submission Format One Slide Submission PDF format Original work only Clear assumptions and supporting data should be mentioned Submission must be made through the Unstop platform within the specified deadline Nature: Elimination Round Only shortlisted teams will qualify for the final round. Round 3 — the Founder's Room Online Presentation | Final Elimination Round You've torn down the business. You've rebuilt it. Now convince the jury that your version is better. details_text: All that you need to know about the Mock IPL Auction “The Ultimate IPL Auction: Build Your Dynasty” Cricket is not just about big names. It is about strategy, budgets, combinations, and making the right call when the pressure is on. Welcome to the Mock IPL Auction, a strategy-driven competition where your team will step into the shoes of an IPL franchise management team. From identifying the right players to managing your purse and building a balanced squad, every decision could define your season. Do you have what it takes to build a championship-winning squad? Bring your cricket knowledge, sharpen your strategic thinking, and get ready to bid, bluff, calculate, and build your dream IPL team. Rewards & Prizes Exciting prizes and rewards for the top-performing teams. Certificates for participating teams. Exclusive goodies and partner benefits for winners and finalists. Recognition for the best auction strategy and squad-building performance. Exact prizes, rewards, and partner benefits will be announced by the organizers. Round 1: The Team Selection Test Mode: Online Format: Quiz Team Size: 2 to 3 members The journey begins with an exciting Cricket Quiz designed to test your knowledge of IPL, international cricket, players, teams, records, and the game beyond the scoreboard. Advancement: The top 10 teams from Round 1 will qualify for the Mock IPL Auction. Round 2: The Mock IPL Auction Mode: Off-Campus Simulation Team Size: 2 to 3 members The real battle begins. The top 10 teams will enter the auction simulation, where every team will be assigned an actual IPL franchise. Build the strongest possible squad for your franchise. Each participating team will receive a fixed purse and will compete in a live IPL-style auction simulation to acquire players. You will need to: Manage your purse strategically Identify valuable players Make smart bidding decisions Build a balanced squad Plan according to your franchise's requirements Adapt to changing auction dynamics Make every bid count The complete auction rules, purse details, player pool, squad requirements, bidding mechanics, and additional conditions will be revealed after Round 1. So come prepared for the unexpected. One reckless bid could drain your purse. One missed opportunity could weaken your squad. One smart acquisition could change everything. The Ultimate Challenge Building a squad is easy, but building the right squad within a limited purse is the real game. Your team will have to balance star power with squad depth, experience with potential, and aggressive bidding with financial discipline. Every player has a price. Every bid has a consequence. Every decision matters. Scoring & Key Considerations Keep these factors in mind throughout the auction: Each player will carry specific points. The remaining purse will also contribute to the final score. Your squad must be completed as per the given requirements. The required numbers of batters, bowlers, all-rounders, international and national players must be maintained. All teams must follow the specified squad and auction requirements. The team with the highest final points will win. All major scoring rules, player points, squad requirements, and category limits will be revealed after Round 1. Eligibility Open to college students. Team size: 2 to 3 members. Inter-college teams may participate. Each team must participate in Round 1 to qualify for Round 2. Only the top 10 teams from Round 1 will advance to the auction simulation. Rules & Guidelines The competition will be conducted across two rounds. Round 1 will be an online quiz. The top 10 teams from Round 1 will qualify for Round 2. Round 2 will be an off-campus IPL auction simulation. Teams will consist of 2 to 3 members. Each qualified team will be assigned an actual IPL franchise. Every team will receive a fixed purse for the auction. Teams must build their complete squad within the allocated purse and according to the rules revealed by the organizers. All players acquired

details_text: Can You Spot What Others Miss?: A 10-Minute Digital Perception Challenge: How carefully do you read what you see online? You will experience a simulated smartphone environment , examine online advertising content, make judgements, and answer a short set of questions. The challenge is designed to test your attention, interpretation, and perception —there are no right or wrong answers. What will be recorded?: The study records: Your responses Time spent on each page Basic demographic information such as age group and gender The study does not record your name, email address, IP address, or location . Your responses are identified using a randomly generated code . Rules of the Challenge: Participation is voluntary . The challenge must be completed individually . Participants should complete the activity in one sitting . Please carefully read every screen and piece of information before proceeding. Do not deliberately skip, rush through, or randomly answer questions. Participants should respond based on their own perceptions and impressions . Do not discuss or share the study materials with other potential participants before they complete the challenge , as this may influence their natural responses. Participants may exit the study at any time before submission. There are no correct or incorrect responses; authentic responses are what matter . The study should not be completed multiple times by the same participant. Why Participate?: This is more than simply answering a questionnaire. For around 10 minutes , you will get the opportunity to step into the role of an everyday digital consumer and see how you respond when advertising and product information are presented online. Your attention matters. Your first impression matters. What you notice—and what you don't—matters. details_text: Fault Hunt: Official Event Rulebook · Concetto 2026: Overview: Fault Hunt is a circuit-analysis and troubleshooting event. Teams find faults in LTspice circuits and justify their findings through systematic analysis. The event has two rounds: Round 1 – Preliminary Individual Quiz Round 2 – Circuit Fault Analysis Prerequisites: Participants must have LTspice installed on their laptop before the event. Windows: Download LTspice macOS: Download LTspice Event Structure: Round 1: Preliminary Quiz — 30 Minutes — Top 10 Teams Round 2: Circuit Fault Analysis (LTspice) — 90 Minutes — — Eligibility & Team Specifications: Open to students from all branches. Team size: 1–3 members. Each team must have a unique team name. A participant may be part of only one team. Teams must remain unchanged throughout the event. Round 1 – Preliminary Quiz: The quiz is conducted individually, not team-wise. Duration: 30 minutes . Questions cover fundamental electronics and circuit analysis. Collaboration between team members during the quiz is not permitted. Team Score = Sum of individual scores ÷ Number of team members The top 10 teams based on this score qualify for Round 2. Round 2 – Circuit Fault Analysis: Duration: 90 minutes . All qualified teams receive the same LTspice circuit files containing intentional faults. Teams must identify the faulty component(s) or connection(s), support the finding with simulation results, and explain the cause. Internet is permitted for datasheets and references only. Teams submit a short fault report along with their LTspice files before time ends. Evaluation Criteria: The emphasis is not only on finding the correct fault, but on how the team reaches it and explains its reasoning. Accuracy of Fault Identification — 30 Troubleshooting Approach & Logical Reasoning — 25 Use of LTspice Simulation & Measurements — 20 Clarity & Quality of Explanation — 15 Handling of Questions — 10 Total — 100 Rules & Regulations: Teams must consist of 1–3 members. Round 1 must be attempted individually by every team member. The top 10 teams qualify for Round 2. Solutions must be the team's own work. Plagiarism, cheating or misconduct may result in disqualification. Judges' decisions are final and binding. The organisers reserve the right to make necessary changes to the schedule or rules. Prizes: Winner — ₹5,000 Runner-up — ₹3,000 Second Runner-up — ₹2,000 Total Prize Pool — ₹10,000 Debug Smart. Find the Fault.

title: Reeliyaapa: Be the Creator!
description: VIJYAPANA REEL CHALLENGE: One Vendor. Everything Marketing. THE CHALLENGE: Businesses today need multiple people for multiple marketing requirements. Social media. Print. PR. Corporate gifting. Photoshoots. Video…
details_text: VIJYAPANA REEL CHALLENGE: One Vendor. Everything Marketing. THE CHALLENGE: Businesses today need multiple people for multiple marketing requirements. Social media. Print. PR. Corporate gifting. Photoshoots. Video production. TV commercials. Branding. Advertising. And much more. That often means different vendors, different calls, different follow-ups and a lot of hassle. But what if one company could handle it all? That's Vijyapana. Your challenge is to create an Instagram Reel that brings this idea to life: “Why manage 10 different vendors when 1 can handle all the hassle?” Show us what Vijyapana does and why having one partner for your branding and marketing requirements makes business easier. BUT THERE'S ONE REQUIREMENT: AI-assisted editing is mandatory. Participants must use AI meaningfully in the editing/post-production of their Reel. But I would not require them to generate the entire video with AI. That's not what you want. We aren't looking for a Reel that is simply shot and edited traditionally. We want to see how well you can use AI as an editing and post-production tool. For example, you can use AI to: Change or enhance lighting. Replace backgrounds or locations. Change a car or other objects. Transform the environment around your subject. Create realistic visual effects. Remove or add elements. Change weather, time of day or surroundings. Generate realistic elements and integrate them into footage. Create seamless AI-assisted transitions. Enhance or modify existing footage. Create realistic composites. The AI should be visible in the execution, not just mentioned in the Reel. Your Reel can be shot anywhere. Kanpur can become Dubai. A normal car can become something else. An ordinary location can become extraordinary. What matters is how convincingly and creatively you execute your idea. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: We are not asking: “Who can make the craziest AI video?” We are asking: “Who can take a simple advertising message and turn it into an exceptional video using AI-assisted editing?” The idea comes first. The editing brings the idea to life. And AI is one of your most important tools. THE CORE MESSAGE: Your Reel must communicate the essence of: Why manage 10 vendors when 1 can handle everything? And that one is Vijyapana. You are free to build your own story around this. It could be: A business owner struggling with multiple vendors. A funny situation involving endless calls. A cinematic transformation. A before/after concept. A visual metaphor. A mini advertisement. A completely unexpected creative concept. There is no fixed storytelling format. But by the end, the viewer should understand: Vijyapana is the one-stop solution for branding and marketing.

title: The Wrecking Ball Challenge
description: The Wrecking Ball Challenge is Techfest, IIT Bombay’s premier autonomous robotics competition . Participants are tasked with designing, building, and deploying a self-contained, autonomous, battery-powered spherical…
details_text: The Wrecking Ball Challenge is Techfest, IIT Bombay’s premier autonomous robotics competition . Participants are tasked with designing, building, and deploying a self-contained, autonomous, battery-powered spherical robot to navigate a high-stakes 75-meter obstacle-laden arena . The challenge evaluates advanced engineering principles—balancing internal mechanical actuation (Center-of-Gravity stabilization) with real-time vision algorithms to autonomously navigate ramps, smash low-density barriers, and evade a swinging pendulum . Do you have what it takes to engineer a rolling sphere that can master autonomous vision-based navigation under pressure ? Benchmark your innovation against the top student teams across the country and compete for cash prizes, internships, and subscriptions! Eligibility & Team Structure Eligibility: Open to all currently enrolled undergraduate, postgraduate, or diploma students from recognized academic institutions . Team Size: Up to 6 members per team . Inter-College Teams: Permitted . Registration: All teams must register on techfest.org to receive an official Team ID . Round Details & Structure Phase 1: Registration & CAD Abstract Submission (Deadline: October 20, 2026) Format: Online Document Submission . Deliverable: Submit a CAD assembly illustrating the internal electronic layout, center-of-gravity placement, system architecture schematic, and dimension compliance . Phase 2: Virtual Design & Simulation Audit (Deadline: November 15, 2026) Format: Virtual Evaluation . Deliverable: Technical Simulation Report including mathematical analysis validating actuator torque across inclined planes (specifically the 0.8 ft ramp), balance stability calculations, and wireless emergency kill-switch implementation . Finalist Announcement: November 20, 2026 . Phase 3: Grand Finale (On-Campus at IIT Bombay — Dec 16–17, 2026) Day 1 (Dec 16): On-Site Technical Inspection & Qualifying Heats Dimensional compliance check (2.0 to 2.5 ft diameter), weight verification, electrical isolation, emergency kill-switch validation, and preliminary practice runs . Day 2 (Dec 17): Official Timed Final Heats Teams execute official timed runs across the 75-meter arena . Teams get 3 restart attempts , with only the top performance logged . The 75-Meter Arena Layout The track is guided visually by color-coded boundary cones ( Red on the right, Yellow on the left) : Sector 1: The Gate Runway (0m–15m): Straight acceleration stretch with wide chevron-patterned cone gates for vision calibration . Sector 2: The Step-Up Ramps (15m–35m): Three consecutive incline ramps (0.2 ft, 0.4 ft, and 0.8 ft heights) . Sector 3: The Wrecking Zone (35m–55m): Low-density barriers (foam, thermocol, cardboard) that the robot must plow through while staying on course . Sector 4: The Pendulum Gauntlet (55m–75m): Final sector featuring a continuously swinging mechanical pendulum before the finish line . Technical & Constraint Guidelines Robot Dimensions: Outer shell must be strictly spherical with a diameter between 2.0 feet and 2.5 feet . Peripheral Limits: External sensors or camera mounts cannot extend more than 0.5 feet beyond the shell surface . Autonomy: 100% autonomous operation; no manual remote control, tethered lines, or external offload processing permitted . Primary Sensing: Onboard camera system must serve as the primary path-tracking sensor (IMUs, encoders, distance sensors permitted internally for balance) . Safety: Must include a working wireless emergency kill switch that halts motor power immediately . Penalties: Touching, knocking over, or running over any boundary cone incurs a +5 second penalty per instance .

title: Business Charades – Rounds & Rules
description: Rounds & Rules: Round 1: Concept in Action: Objective: Shortlist the Top 8 teams. Each team gets 2 chits, one at a time. Each chit contains a business-related brand, app, technology, product, company, personality, or…
details_text: Rounds & Rules: Round 1: Concept in Action: Objective: Shortlist the Top 8 teams. Each team gets 2 chits, one at a time. Each chit contains a business-related brand, app, technology, product, company, personality, or concept. One participant act while the team guesses. Time limit: 60 seconds per chit. The participant cannot speak, mouth words, write, use numbers/alphabets, point at objects, or use external props as clues. No passing or replacement of chits is allowed. Only the intended/correct answer accepted by the judge will be considered. Scoring: 10 points per correct answer. Top 8 teams qualify for Round 2. In case of a tie, a sudden-death charade will be conducted. Round 2: Business Jargons: Objective: Shortlist the Top 4 teams. A business-related statement, situation, image, or video will be displayed. Teams have 30 seconds to press the buzzer. The first registered buzzer gets the opportunity to answer. The selected team gets 10 seconds to answer. No passing is allowed after buzzing. Correct answer: +100 points. Correct answer after clue: +70 points. Incorrect/no answer after buzzing: −25 points. If no team buzzes within 30 seconds, the question is closed. Clue: The team gets an additional 15 seconds; once requested, the clue cannot be withdrawn. Only the specific intended business term will be accepted; generic answers will not be considered. Top 4 teams qualify for Round 3. Ties will be resolved through a tie-breaker question. Round 3: The Business Canon: Stage 1 – Business Pictionary: One team member draws while the rest of the team guesses. Time limit: 60 seconds. Only drawings are permitted. No alphabets, words, numbers, initials, abbreviations, gestures, sounds, or written clues are allowed. The drawing cannot be used to directly spell or indicate the answer. Only one final answer will be accepted. Questions will not be passed to another team. Stage 2 – Yes/No Challenge: One person picks a chit with the business term/brand name/business personality/etc. Teams can ask 25 questions to the team member who has seen the chit. The team member who has seen the chit can answer only with: Yes or No Teams must identify the correct answer within 3 minutes or 25 questions (whichever completes first). The team is allowed a maximum of 3 final guesses. The 4th guess will not be accepted, even if it is correct. No electronic devices are permitted. Team members may discuss among themselves. The challenge ends once the correct answer is given, the question limit is reached, or the time expires.

title: The Management Auction - Decide, Bid, Build.
description: Overview Format: Team Event | Online + Offline: Team Size: 1 – 3 Members Brief In the real world, managers rarely get everything they want. Every decision is a trade-off, and success belongs to those who know what…
details_text: Overview Format: Team Event | Online + Offline: Team Size: 1 – 3 Members Brief In the real world, managers rarely get everything they want. Every decision is a trade-off, and success belongs to those who know what matters most and allocate limited resources accordingly. THE MANAGEMENT AUCTION turns this reality into a competitive game, challenging participants to think like decision-makers, bid like strategists, and defend their choices like leaders. Round 1 – Decision Making: Before managing resources, participants must first show sound judgement. This round presents situational and aptitude-style questions modelled on management entrance examinations, testing how well teams read a situation and arrive at the right call under time pressure. The round will determine which teams advance further. Round 2 – Management Bidding: This round puts strategy and negotiation at the forefront. Each team is handed a business problem and a limited budget with which to bid for resources, including Men, Money, Machine, Material, Technology, Time, and Information. With every resource carrying a different weight, teams must decide what to fight for, what to let go, and how their final combination will create the most value. Final Evaluation – Build: The auction closes and the strategy takes shape. Teams present how their acquired resources come together to solve the business problem, and are judged on the soundness of their allocation, the logic of their strategy, the value they create, and the clarity of their presentation. Rules and Guidelines: Number of Rounds: 2 + Final Evaluation (Decision Making → Management Bidding → Build).. Team Size: [1–3] members per team. All team members must be from the same institution. A student cannot be part of more than one team. Each team may submit only one entry per round. Round 1 responses must be completed within the stipulated window; late entries will not be considered. Round 1 must be attempted independently by the team. Any form of malpractice, use of unfair means, or collaboration with other teams will result in immediate disqualification. Round 2 is mandatory in-person; shortlisted teams unable to attend offline will be removed from the competition. Bidding budgets, resource values, time limits, and auction rules for Round 2 will be shared with shortlisted teams beforehand and must be strictly followed. All bids once placed are final and cannot be withdrawn. Teams may not trade or transfer resources with other teams unless explicitly permitted by the organisers. Any violation of the above rules will result in immediate disqualification of the entire team The event format and rules are subject to change prior to the commencement of the event. All decisions regarding eligibility, shortlisting, and final evaluation shall rest with THE MANAGEMENT AUCTION team and the judges. The judges’ decision shall be final and binding, and no further requests or appeals will be entertained once the results are declared. Eligibility:- Only UG students can particiapte.

details_text: Overview Think Fast. Solve Smart. Make an Impact. Are you ready to enter the realm of tough decisions? Strategy Sprint is a fast-paced challenge that puts your problem-solving, creativity, and decision-making skills to the ultimate test.. Be it entering new markets, formulating successful strategies, handling unexpected problems, or saving struggling companies—every round brings new exciting challenge to tackle. There is no single formula for success. You’ll need to analyse the situation, think beyond the obvious, work as a team, and make bold decisions under pressure. Whether you’re a business enthusiast, an analytical thinker, a creative problem-solver, or simply someone who loves a good challenge, Strategy Sprint is your chance to step up, think differently, and prove what you can do. organiser: Shaheed Rajguru College of Applied Sciences for Women, Delhi University
description: Date of Event is 15 October 2026 Pixel Prompt is a fast-paced game of visual description and AI generation. One team member (the Describer) is shown a secret target image for about 2 minutes to observe and memorize key…
details_text: Date of Event is 15 October 2026 Pixel Prompt is a fast-paced game of visual description and AI generation. One team member (the Describer) is shown a secret target image for about 2 minutes to observe and memorize key details. They must then convey those details to their teammate (the Prompter). Using only those verbal clues, the Prompter constructs a detailed text prompt to generate an image via an AI tool that matches the original photo as closely as possible. The team whose generated image comes closest to the original wins. Duration: 15-30 minutes (adjust based on the event) Guidelines: Team Structure: Every team must consist of exactly 2 members—Member 1 (Describer) and Member 2 (Prompter). Observation Phase: Member 1 will be shown the target image for 2 minutes. Member 2 must look away or remain blindfolded during that time. Communication Phase: Once the time is up, Member 1 has 4 minutes to verbally describe the image to Member 2. No gestures, drawing, or showing written notes are allowed. Prompting Phase: Member 2 will write a prompt into the designated AI image generator within 6 minutes to render the image. Rules and Regulations: Generation Limit: Only one prompt attempt (or a maximum of two, if specified before the event) per round is allowed per team. No Direct Assistance: Member 1 cannot touch the keyboard or assist Member 2 in writing the actual text prompt. Disqualification: Any team caught taking photos, using smartphones during the round, or looking at the target image out of turn will be disqualified immediately. Evaluation criteria: Subject & Core Layout (10 points ): the actual representation of the image generated. Chromatic Fidelity & Color Accuracy (30 points ): measures how closely the generated image reproduces the colors, color relationships, intensity, and overall color mood of the original target image. ⁠Dual Image Comparative Exactness (20 points ): evaluates the side-by-side similarity between the original target image and the AI-generated image. The judge compares both images directly and determines how accurately the generated image reproduces the original. ⁠Prompt Syntax & Descriptive Precision (20 points ):  evaluates how effectively the Prompter converts the Describer's verbal information into a clear, structured, and specific AI prompt. This directly aligns with the event's criterion of evaluating the effectiveness, descriptive detail, and efficiency of the prompt. Background & Environmental Context (20 points ): evaluates how accurately the generated image recreates the surrounding setting and environmental elements of the original image—not just the main subject. This is important because the original Pixel Prompt criteria specifically include similarity in key elements and overall composition. Note: The detailed scoring system and weightage for each criterion will be announced by the event coordinators. About the Event: Digital Design Challenge is an individual competition designed to test participants' knowledge and practical skills in digital logic and Hardware Description Languages (HDLs). The challenge focuses on designing combinational and sequential circuits, FSMs, memory interfaces, and basic digital architectures using Verilog HDL, with the option to support VHDL if enabled by the organisers. Objective: To test participants' understanding of digital logic and RTL design. To develop practical HDL programming skills. To evaluate the ability to design combinational and sequential circuits. To test problem-solving under strict time constraints. To encourage efficient, readable, and synthesis-ready HDL code. To provide practical exposure to digital-system design and simulation. Problem Statement: Participants will be given 10 digital design problems covering combinational logic, sequential circuits, finite state machines, memory interfaces, and basic processor components. Participants must develop correct, synthesis-ready solutions using only Verilog or VHDL within the given time limit. Solutions will be evaluated using suitable HDL simulators and testbenches against predefined or hidden test cases. Event Details: Participants will individually solve 10 HDL-based digital design problems within a fixed time limit of 1 hour . Questions may include: Combinational logic Sequential circuits Counters and registers FSMs Memory interfaces Basic processor components Participants may use only Verilog or VHDL. The challenge will be conducted offline without internet or AI assistance. Evaluation: Submitted solutions will be tested using suitable HDL simulators/compilers against testbenches. Participants will be evaluated based on functional correctness, optimisation, readability, and testbench implementation where applicable. Rules and Regulations: Participation is individual only. Participants must carry a valid student ID. Only Verilog or VHDL is allowed. No other HDL or programming language will be permitted. The competition will be conducted in offline mode. Internet access, mobile phones, and smartwatches are not permitted. No AI assistance is permitted during the challenge. Participants must write all code during the event. Pre-written code snippets, templates, or solutions are not allowed. Plagiarism or use of pre-existing code will result in disqualification. Participants must use the HDL and simulation environment specified by the organisers. Misbehaviour may result in disqualification. The coordinators' decision will be final. Judging Criteria: Functional Correctness – 60% Code Optimisation & Efficiency – 20% Readability & Comments – 10% Testbench Completeness – 10% In case of a tie, higher performance on advanced FSM/sequential-design problems will be considered, followed by submission timestamp. Judge's Decision is Final: The judges' decision will be final and will be based on the specified judging criteria, technical correctness, and overall performance. Eligibility: Open to students from recognised colleges/universities. Participation is allowed individually only. Valid student ID is mandatory. Certification Policy: Certificates will be provided to all participants. Certificate of Excellence will be awarded to winners as per judges' results. About the Event: The Arduino Uno is an open-source microcontroller board based on the Microchip ATmega328P, widely used for building interactive electronic systems. It features 14 digital input/output pins, 6 analog inputs, a 16 MHz clock, and a USB interface, making it easy to connect with various sensors and actuators. In embedded automation projects like smart dustbins, the Arduino Uno acts as the central control unit-processing data from proximity and moisture sensors to operate servo motors for automatic lid opening and waste segregation. Its user-friendly ecosystem, affordability, and extensive community support make it an ideal choice for rapid hardware prototyping. Objective: To encourage practical application of embedded-system concepts. To develop solutions for real-world student-related problems. To test sensor interfacing and microcontroller programming skills. To encourage efficient real-time data processing and decision-making. To promote creativity and hardware-software co-design. To develop participants' ability to plan and implement a solution within a defined problem statement. Problem Statement: Improper segregation of wet and dry waste at the source makes waste management, recycling, and disposal difficult. People often fail to dispose of waste into its respective dustbin due to negligence or lack of awareness. The proposed project aims to develop an Arduino-based smart dustbins that automatically opens when waste is detected, identifies the waste category using sensors, and directs compatible waste to the appropriate compartment. Non-compatible waste is automatically rejected, reducing contamination and eliminating the need for manual segregation. Event Structure: Stage 1 – Ideation & Problem Validation: Teams identify a real-world problem and define their proposed solution, target users, and value proposition. Stage 2 – Final Presentation & Evaluation: Teams demonstrate their working prototype and present their technical architecture, implementation, and solution. The final presentation consists of a 10-minute pitch followed by 5 minutes of Q&A with the judging panel. Detection & Automation : The system must detect both wet and dry waste and open automatically upon waste detection. title: Build for AI Agents: LLM SkillHub Challenge 2026
description: Build for AI Agents: LLM SkillHub Student Challenge 2026 AI is moving from chatbots to AI agents that actually get work done. But agents still waste tokens, lose track of multi-step workflows, and need the same…
details_text: Build for AI Agents: LLM SkillHub Student Challenge 2026 AI is moving from chatbots to AI agents that actually get work done. But agents still waste tokens, lose track of multi-step workflows, and need the same instructions again and again. This challenge asks you to fix that by teaching an agent a skill. The Challenge Build a skill: a reusable set of instructions (a SKILL.md file, plus optional scripts and reference files) that teaches an AI agent to do one specific task better, faster and more reliably. Skills work with agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and opencode. Your skill can help with anything: coding, research, education, productivity, data analysis, career guidance, automation, or a problem specific to India. You don't need to build an app or train a model. Teach an existing agent something useful. What You'll Do Pick a real-world problem, ideally one you have seen up close. Build an AI-agent skill that solves it. Publish it as a PUBLIC skill on LLM SkillHub (llmskillhub.com). (Optional, good to have) Create evaluation cases that define what "good" looks like, and run them. Test your skill with real users and improve it based on their feedback. Submit your entry here on Unstop. What to Submit The link to your public skill on LLM SkillHub A short write-up (up to 500 words): the problem, who has it, how your skill solves it, and what you changed after testing User feedback: how many people tried it and what they said Optional, but good to have: your eval and its results, and a demo video of up to 2 minutes Important Your skill must be public. Skills kept in a private space can't be judged. Provide the email ID linked to your LLM SkillHub account on the Unstop registration form (you sign in to LLM SkillHub with Google or GitHub). Publish early: every public skill is reviewed by a person before it is listed. Each participant can submit as many as skills they feel like, no restrictions on number of skills submitted. Judging Criteria Real-world usefulness Quality and reliability of the skill Problem-solving and originality Documentation and usability Feedback from real users Evaluation performance (if you include an eval) What You Get A certificate for everyone with a valid submission Top 10: T-shirt + Sipper + Keychain Ranks 11–20: T-shirt Mentorship from industry experts for the best skills that target a real problem and solve it Preference for future internship opportunities for winners (a preference, not a guaranteed selection) Your skill published and showcased on LLM SkillHub A real AI-agent project for your portfolio An open-source skill other developers and AI-agent users can actually use Goodies go only to the top 20 skill publishers as ranked by the judges, and mentorship only to the best skills; not every participant receives them. Who Can Participate College students across India who are interested in AI, software development, automation, research, productivity, or building useful technology. You don't have to be an AI/ML expert. What matters most is finding a useful problem and building a skill that solves it well.

details_text: The Finance and Investment Cell of Jesus and Mary College is proud to present the fourth edition of Bahulya , a premier finance case competition that challenges participants to showcase their analytical acumen, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills. This year’s edition explores one of the world’s biggest sporting spectacles through a financial lens: the feasibility of hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030 in India . Participants will be required to navigate the complexities of large-scale infrastructure investment, financing, revenue generation, commercial opportunities, and long-term economic viability. This Year’s Theme: The Feasibility of Hosting the FIFA World Cup in India India is evaluating the feasibility of hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030, presenting an ambitious opportunity to combine sporting development with large-scale economic and infrastructural growth. Participants will assess whether the potential economic and social value generated by the tournament can justify the significant investment required. The case will require teams to evaluate market demand, revenue potential, capital expenditure, financing structures, host cities, infrastructure, commercial innovation, social impact, risk management, and post-event utilisation. Teams will be expected to build a financially sound and strategically viable roadmap for hosting the tournament while ensuring that the infrastructure and investments remain sustainable beyond 2030. No prior knowledge of FIFA is required, only strong financial reasoning, strategic thinking, creativity, and the ability to make data-driven decisions. Guidelines: Teams of 1–4 participants. All rounds are eliminative. Open to all undergraduate students of the University of Delhi, across colleges, years, and disciplines. Cross-college and cross-discipline teams are permitted. Strict no-plagiarism policy applies. Participants must clearly state their assumptions and justify their financial projections and strategic recommendations. Adherence to the prescribed submission format and guidelines is mandatory.

details_text: Real-World Business Case Challenge: "Solve a problem that exists in the real world" Solve. Strategize. Create Impact. For example: Case Theme: "How can a growing company increase its market presence and customer acquisition while competing with established players?" title: LinkedIn Launchpad: Build Your Professional Brand
description: About the Competition In today’s digital-first professional world, your online presence is becoming as important as your resume . A strong personal brand can help you get noticed, build credibility, connect with the…
details_text: About the Competition In today’s digital-first professional world, your online presence is becoming as important as your resume . A strong personal brand can help you get noticed, build credibility, connect with the right people, and create opportunities even before you formally apply for them. Platforms like LinkedIn and Instagram are no longer just social media platforms . LinkedIn has become a powerful space for professional networking, recruitment, thought leadership, and career opportunities, while Instagram has evolved into an important platform for personal branding, content creation, community building, and showcasing your personality, skills, and interests. Your resume may get you a foot in the door, but your digital presence can determine whether people remember you, trust you, and want to connect with you. Whether you are a student looking for internships, a fresher searching for your first opportunity, or a professional building industry connections, having a strong and authentic personal brand can significantly strengthen your professional journey. LinkedIn Launchpad is designed to help participants understand the importance of social media in today's professional ecosystem and express ideas, build credibility, and express your POV. The competition will challenge you to think about real-world issues, form your own opinions, and communicate those opinions effectively through LinkedIn. It is not just about what you think - it is about how you communicate, how you present, and how effectively you can build your professional voice online. Make sure you join the competition group for further updates and instructions. Competition Format Round : Professional Opinion & LinkedIn Writing Challenge Participants will be given 7 different topics based on common issues faced by youth. These topics will be posted over InteractUp's Linkedin. Make sure to join the competition group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/B5aO6OWtJN78PNl7fgq0NI For each topic, participants will be required to: Develop their own thoughts, opinions, and perspectives on the given issue. Write their response in a manner suitable for a professional LinkedIn audience. Publish/repost their written response on LinkedIn as instructed. Demonstrate their ability to communicate ideas clearly, creatively, and professionally. The objective is not simply to write about a topic, but to demonstrate how effectively you can form an opinion, communicate it, and create meaningful professional content that contributes to your personal brand. Submission Guidelines Individual participation only. All content must be original and based on the participant's own thoughts and perspectives. Responses must maintain professional and respectful language. Participants must repost the given problem on LinkedIn along with their own thoughts and perspectives, as instructed. Judging Criteria Participants will be judged on the quality and originality of their thoughts, creativity, clarity of communication, relevance of their perspective, professional presentation, and overall effectiveness of their content and personal branding. Rewards & Benefits Top 25 participants will receive: 6 Months of LinkedIn Premium Career at just ₹2,400 (original value: ₹11,100 ). Exclusive Master Session Series by InteractUp , specially designed to enhance soft skills, worth ₹9,400 . Special LinkedIn Growth Paid Group access worth ₹2,100 , provided completely free. Total benefits worth ₹20,200 per participant, with a total prize value of ₹5,05,000 for the Top 25 participants. Important Note This competition is created purely for educational and professional development purposes. It aims to encourage participants to develop their professional voice, personal brand, and digital presence , understand real-world issues, and effectively leverage platforms such as LinkedIn and Instagram for networking, career growth, content creation, and professional opportunities. title: Google Cloud: Learn with Communities-Developer (Professionals)
description: Google Cloud: Learn with Communities is a hands-on learning program forvdevelopers who want to build real skills on Google Cloud. You follow a curated skill badge curriculum, work through guided labs on Google Skills,…
details_text: Google Cloud: Learn with Communities is a hands-on learning program forvdevelopers who want to build real skills on Google Cloud. You follow a curated skill badge curriculum, work through guided labs on Google Skills, and earn badges that show what you can do. Eligibility Criteria: Open to working professionals. Pre-Registration Checklist: Complete the following before filling out the enrolment form: Active Google Skills Account: Have an active Google Skills account and keep your account email address ready. Ensure that you provide a NEW Google Skills Account link created after 14th September, 2026 . Otherwise, your candidature will not be accepted. Only badges completed during the program window will be counted. If you haven't completed any badges from your respective curriculum, you can use your existing account. If you've already completed some or all badges, we recommend creating a new Google Skills account with a different email address . Public Google Skills Profile: Set your Google Skills profile to Public and keep your profile URL ready. Watch the how-to video Developers Only - GEAR Program: Sign up for the GEAR Program and keep your Google Developer profile URL ready. Video Instructions | PDF Guide Program Structure: 1 - Create A New Active Google Skills Account Sign up for a NEW active Google Skills account with a fresh email, then set your profile to Public so you can share your profile URL. Watch how to make your profile public → Only new accounts created after 14th September are eligible to receive skill badges — so make sure you sign up on a fresh account for the campaign. 2 - Fill The Enrolment Form Register through the competition page and enter Unstop as your partner along with the referral code KTQW48 . Developers (working professionals) should also provide their GEAR/Google Developer profile URL . 3 - Receive Your Enrolment Email Once your enrolment is processed, you'll get a confirmation email with your unique access code . Hang tight - this is sent after registrations are collected, so expect a wait of 7–10 days . 4 - Redeem Your Access Code Open an incognito window , follow the redemption link, and enter your access code. Sign in to Google Skills, and you'll see 9 credits ready to go. Follow the walkthrough video → Your access code is personal, works once, and can't be shared. Use the exact link from your email — searching the catalogue won't work. 5 - Complete Your First Lab & Keep Going Open "A Tour of Google Cloud Hands-on Labs" and click Start Lab . Follow the steps, spend at least 6 minutes , and aim for a score of 100 . When you're done, click End Lab — the 200 free credits are added automatically ; no extra claim needed. Check your balance at skills.google/my_account/credits . Then work through your curriculum and rack up badges. Credits and badges: 9 Google Skills Credits: Unlocked when you redeem your access code. 200 Google Skills Credits: Credited once you complete "A Tour of Google Cloud Hands-on Labs ". Google Cloud Skill Badges: Earned by completing the curriculum for your track Rewards: Google-branded Certificate — Receive a certificate from Google upon successful completion of the course/curriculum. Note: In case of any queries, please reach out to learnwithcommunities-support@google.com . Include screenshots and a short description of the problem. You’re all set! Now it’s time to dive in, complete your labs, and make the most of the learning journey. Happy learning!

Market Maestros 2026 is a Stock Market Simulation & Investment Challenge organised by Krtyanvesana – The Consulting Club, Institute of Management Studies, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), with Motilal Oswal and Dhanalytics AI as the Title Sponsors. Experience the dynamics of financial markets, analyse market movements, make strategic investment decisions and put your market acumen to the test. What is Market Maestros: Market Maestros is a simulated stock market competition that gives participants an opportunity to experience investing and trading in a competitive environment. Participants will analyse market situations, manage their virtual portfolios and make strategic decisions while balancing risk and potential returns. Competition Structure: Round 1 — Stock Market Simulation: A one-week trading and investment simulation where teams analyse market movements and manage their virtual portfolios. Round 2 — Investment Strategy Presentation: Shortlisted teams will present their investment strategy, portfolio decisions and market rationale before the judging panel. Eligibility: Open to college and university students across India with an interest in stock markets, finance, investing, business and strategy. Rules and Regulations: Trading platform/software: Arthhwise App will be provided for the trading simulation. Market: Participants can trade/invest only in Indian equity stocks , on a cash basis . Not allowed: Margin/leverage, Futures, Options, Commodities, ETFs, and Mutual Funds. Each team will receive ₹10 lakh virtual capital and login credentials for the Arthhwise App. Title Sponsors: Motilal Oswal & Dhanalytics AI Event Date: 24 October 2026 Join the challenge. Build your strategy. Make your move. Become a Market Maestro.

details_text: Sun Pharma, India’s #1 Pharma Company, is thrilled to launch the second season of PRISM (Pharma Reimagined: Innovation, Strategy & Marketing), an exciting idea challenge for top B-Schools across India. Sun Pharma has built its legacy on innovation, quality, and impact. With SUN PRISM Season 2, we invite the brightest minds from select colleges to solve real-world business challenges and nurture them towards innovation and problem-solving. This challenge offers students a platform to showcase strategic thinking, analytical ability, and problem-solving skills, while interacting with leaders from Sun Pharma. Members from Finalist Teams also stand a chance to secure Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) opportunities for Sun Pharma’s flagship program, which will be extended to winners and runners-up for the SUNRISE Management Trainee Program at Sun Pharma, subject to eligibility criteria, making this a unique opportunity to kick-start your career with the #1 Pharma Company in India. Sun Pharma operates across 100+ countries with a focus on creating access to affordable medicines, innovation-driven growth, and a commitment to excellence. Through SUN PRISM, we are looking for curious, proactive, and solution-oriented individuals who can craft impactful strategies in areas like Marketing, Market Insights, and innovative solutions that can address real-world business opportunities. Eligibility Criteria Open to 2nd-year MBA students pursuing a 2-year full-time flagship MBA from select Institutes. The participants would be able to register with only their Institute email ID. Students currently pursuing part-time, distance learning, integrated courses, and 1 year/executive MBA programs from these institutes are not eligible to participate. Team Structure All participating teams should consist of 3 members. One person cannot be a member of more than one team. All the team members must be from the same institute, and they can be a mix of students from different specializations i.e., cross-specialization teams are allowed. Competition Structure: Virtual Case Study Launch Webinar: Participants will get to know the legacy of Sun Pharma and gain insights into the case study problem statement. Participants will have the opportunity to interact with industry leaders and get their queries addressed during the Q&A session . Executive Summary Submission Round: Registered teams will work on the selected case study and submit a 2-slide PowerPoint presentation outlining their initial ideas and approach. The case files and submission templates can be downloaded from the respective round. Please submit your files in this naming convention only: Leader's First Name_Team Name_Institute Name. Submissions can be uploaded only in .ppt/.pptx/.pdf format. Please ensure that the file size is less than 20 MB. SUN PRISM Brand Quiz: This round will consist of brand-based questions designed to test knowledge around Sun Pharma - its brands, products, key milestones, and presence in the pharmaceutical industry . This will be a non-eliminatory round. Top teams will receive exciting goodies. Detailed Submission Round: Shortlisted teams will expand their initial submission into a comprehensive solution with an implementation roadmap, submitting a 7–10 slide PowerPoint presentation and an optional 2-3 minute video pitch.
